cards.def: A container for patterns and directory numbers. Without a partition in the caller's CSS, the pattern is invisible.
A calling search space is an ordered list of partitions that decides which destinations a caller may reach.

cards.term: CSS is searched first when a phone and a line both have one
cards.def: The directory number CSS takes precedence over the device CSS. The Feature Configuration Guide for Release 15 says so, and the 12.x SRND places the line CSS in front.
The combined partition list in one CSS is limited to 1024 characters, including separators. Long names reduce how many partitions fit.

cards.term: a translation pattern do after it matches
cards.def: It transforms digits and performs another lookup using the CSS configured on the translation pattern.

cards.term: put emergency patterns in a base partition on the device CSS
cards.def: The line CSS can be restrictive and 911 is still reachable, because the device CSS is still concatenated.
Standard Local Route Group selects the egress gateway associated with the calling device's device pool, so one route pattern can serve many sites.

cards.term: Who owns configuration writes in a cluster
cards.def: The publisher, the first node, owns configuration writes. Subscribers do call processing when the Cisco CallManager service is active.

cards.term: What breaks if the publisher is unreachable
cards.def: Configuration changes stop. Calls already hosted on subscribers can continue. Do not treat that as a full cluster failure.
+E.164 is the primary numeric address. Shorter dialing habits are translations on top of it.
The @ wildcard expands to NANP patterns. A route filter such as AREA-CODE narrows them. The unfiltered count is TODO-verify on the Release 15 page. Do not quote 166 unless that page prints it.

cards.term: can DNA and a trunk disagree
cards.def: The Release 15 guide says Dialed Number Analyzer can select the wrong calling-party transformation. Trust the trunk trace.

cards.term: What replaced Call Home as the preferred Smart Licensing transport
cards.def: Smart Transport, from 15SU2. Call Home is deprecated. The product still falls back if smartreceiver.cisco.com is unreachable.

cards.term: a device pool for, in one sentence
cards.def: A device pool binds a phone to a region, a location, a Unified CM group, a date/time group, and the local route group.

cards.term: class of service on Unified CM
cards.def: Partitions plus calling search spaces. There is no separate class-of-service object.

cards.term: must a block pattern be at least as specific as the route it blocks
cards.def: Best match wins on digits. CSS order breaks ties. A short block loses to a longer route pattern.

cards.term: Use Originator's Calling Search Space for
cards.def: Use Originator's Calling Search Space is how a normalization translation keeps the caller's class of service on the second lookup. Confirm the Release 15 checkbox label in the online help before you teach the exact words.
A route list is an ordered list of route groups. The route pattern points at the list, not at a single gateway.
A route group is a set of gateways or trunks that share a distribution algorithm, such as top-down or circular.

cards.term: does time-of-day routing change a partition
cards.def: Time-of-day routing changes a partition when the partition has a time schedule. Outside the schedule the partition is skipped.

cards.term: the first four inbound SIP dial-peer tests.
cards.def: incoming uri via, then request, then to, then from. Cisco's CUBE dial-peer guide for IOS XE 17.6 lists them in that order.

cards.term: What comes after URI matching on an inbound SIP peer
cards.def: URI: incoming called-number, then answer-address. The Cisco IOS call-routing document then lists destination-pattern against the calling number, and dial-peer 0 if nothing matches.
Dial-peer 0 is the default peer. It ignores the codec list, DTMF method, and SIP profile you configured on real peers.

cards.term: is Early Offer configured on Unified CM
cards.def: On the SIP Profile, field Early Offer support for voice and video calls. Best Effort (no MTP inserted) does not insert an MTP to force the offer. The 11.x SRND is the write-up; re-check the label on Release 15.
488 means the remote side rejected the session description. Compare m-lines and codecs on both legs.

cards.term: avoid debug ccsip messages on a busy CUBE
cards.def: CUBE: It can spike CPU. VoIP trace is the safer first look on IOS XE 17.3.2 and 17.4.1a and later.

cards.term: cause 188 often mean on a server-group
cards.def: Cause 188 means Options keepalive marked the target down, so the peer is busied out.
Unsolicited SIP that would become a paid call. The signaling source must be trusted, and the dial peers must still be explicit.

cards.term: Delayed offer to early offer: where is the answer
cards.def: Delayed offer: If CUBE offers early toward the provider, the provider answers in a response, and the original caller may still owe an answer in the ACK if its own leg was delayed.

cards.term: a SIP profile on CUBE for
cards.def: SIP profile: Header and SDP edits on one leg, such as rewriting a=inactive to a=sendrecv when a provider requires it.

cards.term: Two legs means what on a trace
cards.def: An inbound dial peer and an outbound dial peer. Fix the inbound tag before you argue about the outbound pattern.
Expressway-C, the traversal client, opens toward Expressway-E, the traversal server.
_collab-edge._tls, typically port 8443, pointing at Expressway-E.

cards.term: SRV record must not be published externally
cards.def: _cisco-uds._tcp. That name is for clients already inside, so they find Unified CM directly.

cards.term: What must the Expressway-E certificate SAN contain
cards.def: Expressway-E certificate SAN: The public discovery names clients use, including the collab-edge domain. Private .local names do not belong there.

cards.term: does Expressway-C's CA need to live for MRA
cards.def: In Unified CM tomcat-trust and CallManager-trust, followed by the service restarts the MRA guide names.
A traversal zone is the UC traversal relationship between C and E. Both sides must trust the other's certificate chain.

cards.term: does mutual TLS on 5061 break MRA
cards.def: MRA and mutual TLS on the SIP trunk port are incompatible in the Cisco Live and product guidance this lab cites. Do not enable both and expect registration.

cards.term: an expired Expressway-E cert look like
cards.def: Expired Expressway-E cert: External clients fail TLS before any Unified CM login. On-premises phones that never use collab-edge keep working.

cards.term: Dual NIC on Expressway-E: what is the classic IM&P trap
cards.def: XCP traffic can hairpin or black-hole if the internal and external interfaces are not the ones the dual-NIC guide describes.

cards.term: What two duties does Kari's Law put on an MLTS
cards.def: Kari's Law: Direct 911 with no prefix, and notification to a central on-site point when 911 is dialed.

cards.term: Who does Kari's Law apply to
cards.def: Kari's Law applies to multi-line telephone systems manufactured, imported, first sold or leased, or installed after 16 February 2020. The FCC states the rules are forward-looking.
A dispatchable location is the validated street address of the caller plus additional information such as suite, floor, or room.

cards.term: did fixed on-premises MLTS devices have to send automated dispatchable location
cards.def: Dispatchable location: 6 January 2021, under the FCC rules for RAY BAUM'S Act, 47 CFR 9.16.

cards.term: did non-fixed and off-premises MLTS devices come due
cards.def: Off-premises: 6 January 2022. Automated location when technically feasible; otherwise a manual update or the alternative location the rule allows.
An emergency response location: the zone Emergency Responder tracks, such as a switch port, access point, subnet, or a manual assignment.
An ELIN is a DID that represents that ERL toward the PSAP so a callback can return to the right place, including for extension-only users.

cards.term: does CER learn where a phone is
cards.def: CER: Switch port, access point, IP subnet, or a manual configuration. It then passes ALI or ELIN data toward the national provider.

cards.term: HELD in the Release 15 RedSky chapter
cards.def: The endpoint stores a location URI from the RedSky server. Unified CM puts that URI in a Geolocation header and routes the emergency INVITE to RedSky.
The Release 15 guide says RedSky replaces the identity with the right ELIN and sends the call to the PSAP, and can notify by SMS, email, and a security-desk alert.

cards.term: Is a 911 route pattern the same as compliance
cards.def: Route pattern: No. The pattern only selects a route. Location, notification, and direct dial are separate duties.
A test number. Webex's emergency-calling article says to test 933 before you rely on 911. It returns the caller ID and the known address.

cards.term: Does Webex Calling ELIN replace RedSky
cards.def: No. The ELIN help article says ELIN does not change RedSky or PIDF-LO routing. It supplies a callback number from the location's pool.

cards.term: What DSCP does the Collaboration 14 PA assign to audio
cards.def: EF, which is DSCP 46, including the audio of a video call.

cards.term: What DSCP does that PA assign to prioritized room and desktop video
cards.def: AF41, DSCP 34.

cards.term: What DSCP does that PA assign to Jabber, MRA, and edge video
cards.def: AF42, DSCP 36, or AF41 if the enterprise will not keep an opportunistic video class.
CS3, DSCP 24.
The maximum audio codec and the video bit rate between devices. It does not meter how many calls fit on a WAN link.
How much bandwidth Enhanced Locations CAC will admit between two locations.

cards.term: much does a G.711 or G.722 call deduct in the PA model
cards.def: G.711: 80 kbps: 64 kbps of codec plus 16 kbps of IP and UDP overhead.

cards.term: A 384 kbps video call with 64 kbps audio: how does the PA split the pools
cards.def: 384: 320 kbps from the video pool and 80 kbps from the audio pool, when audio of a video call is deducted from the audio pool.

cards.term: service parameter does that split depend on
cards.def: Service parameter: Deduct Audio Bandwidth from Audio Pool for Video Call, under Call Admission Control on the CallManager service.
Hub_None is the default location. Devices that stay there share its links, which is how a phone silently uses the wrong bandwidth budget.

cards.term: Are intra-location bandwidth limits on by default
cards.def: No. The PA says intra-location bandwidth is unlimited by default and should stay that way, because a location represents a LAN.

cards.term: Does LBM follow OSPF when a WAN link fails
cards.def: OSPF: No. Enhanced Locations CAC is a static model. Weights pick one effective path and do not move when the network reconverges.
AAR: When ELCAC denies the call for lack of bandwidth. The PA says it does not run because the WAN is down or the phone is unregistered, and it applies to intra-cluster endpoint calls.

cards.term: do you mark traffic the PA trusts
cards.def: PA: At the access edge. Phones that mark EF and AF41 can be trusted; soft clients often need a re-mark policy.

cards.term: the three PSTN choices in the Webex Calling migration design article.
cards.def: Cisco Calling Plans, Cloud Connected PSTN, and premises PSTN through a local gateway.
A local gateway is the SBC, often CUBE on IOS XE, that connects Webex Calling to a premises trunk or to Unified CM during coexistence.

cards.term: Unified CM SIP port does the local-gateway guide use toward Webex Calling
cards.def: The guide's coexistence example sends Unified CM calls that should reach Webex Calling at the local gateway on port 5065, and PSTN calls on 5060. The trunk security profile must allow 5065.

cards.term: Can one Cisco IOS router be both local gateway and survivability gateway
cards.def: Yes. Webex documents colocation on Cisco IOS managed gateways. High availability is not supported for that local-gateway colocation, and a third-party local gateway does not host survivability.
A survivability gateway is where phones at the site register and keep basic calling when Webex Calling cannot be reached.

cards.term: the Control Hub migration import start from
cards.def: Unified CM Bulk Administration tar files: users and devices. You map device pools toward Webex locations.

cards.term: Do partition names move to Webex Calling
cards.def: No. Webex Calling class of service is locations, calling permissions, and digit patterns, not Unified CM partitions.

cards.term: What should you keep from the Unified CM dial plan
cards.def: Unified CM: +E.164 as the stored address. Extension habits are a site dial plan, not a second identity.

cards.term: does a Webex route group live
cards.def: BRKCOL-2065: a route group is not inside a location. It holds trunks used for premises breakout.

cards.term: Dedicated Instance, next to this migration
cards.def: Dedicated Instance is Unified CM hosted by Cisco. It is not the same project as moving users onto Webex Calling multi-tenant. Do not promise customer-managed limits inside it without the DI guide.

cards.term: What stays on Unified CM during a phased move
cards.def: Unified CM: Users you have not migrated, contact-center route points, and any analog or special device the migration report excludes. Size the local-gateway trunk for the calls that still cross.

cards.term: INVITE without SDP is which offer model
cards.def: INVITE: Delayed offer.

cards.term: INVITE with SDP is which offer model
cards.def: INVITE: Early offer.
100 Trying means a hop received the INVITE. It is not ringing and not an answer.
180 Ringing means the far end is alerting. Media may or may not be present. 183 is the early-media progress response.

cards.term: is the SDP answer in a delayed-offer call
cards.def: Delayed-offer: Often in the ACK, after the 200 carried the offer.
404 means the number was not found at that hop. On CUBE that is often a failed outbound dial peer, not a carrier rejection.
486 means busy here. The user or the trunk refused because the target is busy, not because digits failed to match.
503 means the next hop is unavailable. On CUBE, check server-group keepalive before you blame Unified CM routing.
P-Asserted-Identity. A provider may want the calling number there rather than in From. Confirm which header that provider bills.

cards.term: What fails first when an Expressway-E certificate expires
cards.def: Expressway-E: The TLS handshake from outside clients. Unified CM registration inside the building is a different path.
A chain gap is the server certificate's issuer name is not the subject of the next certificate you installed.

cards.term: is a private root on Expressway-E a design error
cards.def: Expressway-E: Internet clients do not trust your lab CA. The public edge needs a public chain.

cards.term: the cert-chain lab refuse to do
cards.def: The cert-chain lab does not check signatures or private keys. It checks names, dates, SAN entries, and issuer links you supply.
T302 is the interdigit timeout. The 12.x SRND describes a 15 second default and a 4 second floor. Re-check the value on a Release 15 cluster before you quote it as current.
A hunt pilot is a pattern that distributes a call across a line group. It still has to live in a partition the caller can see.
An extension mobility is a user profile logged into a phone. The line CSS comes from the profile, the device CSS from the phone.
Dial-peer group is an outbound steering list hung on the inbound peer, which BRKCOL-2078 uses so direction depends on who started the call.
An options keepalive is SIP OPTIONS sent to a server-group target. Failure busies the target out. That is the usual cause-188 story.

cards.term: What port does the X15.2 MRA guide name for media toward Expressway-E
cards.def: Expressway-E: UDP 36002 through 59999, plus SIP 5061, HTTPS 8443, and XMPP 5222. Re-check the range on the release you operate.

cards.term: a traversal client versus a traversal server
cards.def: A traversal client versus a traversal server is the client (C) initiates. The server (E) listens. Firewalls then only need to allow the outbound connection from C plus the inbound services on E.

cards.term: Off-premises CER users: ELIN or DID
cards.def: The CER national-provider guide says off-premises locations with no infrastructure visibility are sent against the user DID, not an on-prem ELIN.

cards.term: mark audio of a video call as EF in the PA, not AF41
cards.def: AF41: So voice stays in the priority queue even when the call also has video. You then have to deduct that audio from the audio CAC pool or you will over-admit.
An effective path is the single location-link path LBM chooses by cumulative weight. Equal weights make the choice unstable. Set weight so only one path is best.

cards.term: a Webex Calling location, compared with a Unified CM location
cards.def: A Webex location is a site for numbers, emergency address, and PSTN choice. A Unified CM location is a CAC bandwidth object. They share a word and not a database.
SRST: A branch router registers the phones when they lose the cluster, with a smaller dial plan. It is not a second publisher.

cards.term: does a forwarded call reach voicemail
cards.def: Unity Connection routing rules, direct versus forwarded. The CSS that forwards must be able to reach the voicemail pilot.

cards.term: Does IM and Presence choose a PSTN route
cards.def: PSTN: No. It is a subscriber application for presence and chat. Call routing stays on Unified CM.
A PSAP is Public Safety Answering Point. The 911 center that receives the call and the location.
B2BUA: CUBE is a back-to-back user agent: it terminates one SIP dialog and creates another, so the two legs can differ.
A media relay when the client cannot send RTP directly. A static-NAT defect on TURN is a known class of one-way media.
A route filter is a clause that shrinks the @ wildcard so you do not install the entire NANP. Keep the associated pattern count inside the guide's limit.

cards.term: trust store does a phone use to decide Unified CM is genuine
cards.def: Trust store: The ITL, and the CTL if the cluster is mixed mode. An Expressway problem does not empty the ITL.

cards.term: upload a CSV back to Unified CM at the end of the migration flow
cards.def: Control Hub builds a manifest of devices to move. Cloud-Connected UC can pick that up, or you upload the CSV in Unified CM Bulk Administration.
EF: A priority queue, policed to the voice budget. AF41 and AF42 belong in a bandwidth queue, with AF42 dropped first if you keep both.

cards.term: on-site notification mean under Kari's Law
cards.def: On-site notification means someone at the site, such as a security desk, learns that 911 was dialed so they can direct responders. A route pattern alone does not send that notice.

cards.term: Outbound dial-peer tools the CUBE guide names
cards.def: Dial-peer: destination route-string, destination URI, and destination-pattern. Default hunt, as of the call-routing note retrieved 2026-10-14, is scheme 0: longest match, then preference, then random.
A digit analysis is the Unified CM step that takes the dialed string, the effective CSS, and the best matching pattern, then applies a translation or a route.

cards.term: RedSky company ID: where does Webex Calling store it
cards.def: Webex Calling: Control Hub, in the emergency calling / RedSky settings, along with the secret. Phones then learn the LIS address from their config.

cards.term: What happens if video CAC is exhausted and AAR is not configured
cards.def: The call is denied or a video call may drop to audio if the region and the retry settings allow it. Do not assume AAR exists.

cards.term: MRA registration fails and on-prem phones are fine. First DNS check
cards.def: From outside, resolve _collab-edge._tls. From inside, resolve _cisco-uds._tcp. A client on the corporate LAN that finds collab-edge is a split-DNS bug.

cards.term: a calling permission in Webex Calling
cards.def: A calling permission is the class-of-service knob: internal, local, national, international, and similar. It replaces the line CSS block patterns.
Route pattern: A gateway, a trunk, or a route list. The Release 15 call-routing chapter recommends a route list rather than a bare gateway.

cards.term: What may a route list contain
cards.def: Route list: Only route groups, including local route groups. Not gateways directly.
Devices. One device may be in more than one route group.

cards.term: Can a gateway used directly on a route pattern also sit in a route group
cards.def: No. The call-routing chapter says a gateway used directly cannot also be in a route group, and the reverse.

cards.term: the dot in a route pattern
cards.def: A zero-width PreDot marker. It is not a dialed digit.
One digit.
One or more digits, and it waits for the interdigit timer unless the pattern is urgent.
So a pattern that uses ! does not hold 911 on the interdigit timer.
The CSS on a device pool, gateway, or trunk that normalizes the calling number. Release 15 calling-party normalization.
The route filter keeps NANP patterns whose area code is 515. The filter is how you stop @ from matching the world.

cards.term: can DNA and the trunk disagree on the calling number
cards.def: On the calling number, the Release 15 guide says Dialed Number Analyzer can select the wrong calling-party transformation. Trust the trunk trace.
Longest match, then explicit preference, then random. Default, as of the IOS XE call-routing note retrieved 2026-10-14.
A lower preference number means it is tried first when the match length ties.
huntstop means that after a failure on that dial peer, the gateway does not try the next peer.
CUBE: IPv4 and IPv6 session targets and voice class server-group addresses. As of the hardening guide retrieved 2026-10-14.

cards.term: no ip address trusted authenticate do
cards.def: no ip address trusted authenticate accepts any inbound SIP source. It is how toll fraud starts, not a fix.

cards.term: show ip address trusted list show
cards.def: Static entries and dynamic session targets. Dynamic entries drop when the peer is shut or keepalive-down.
Destination dial-peer group is an outbound set attached to the inbound peer. Peers outside the group are not used.

cards.term: do you run debug ccsip messages
cards.def: After VoIP trace, for the call you are watching, and then you remove it. It can hurt a busy border.
A voice class codec is a named codec list a dial peer offers, so you stop advertising every codec the way dial-peer 0 does.

cards.term: CUBE platforms did Microsoft list for Teams Direct Routing as of 2026-10-14
cards.def: 2026-10-14: ISR 1000, ISR 4000, CSR 1000V, ASR 1000, and Catalyst 8000. Re-check the page. Versions live on that page.

cards.term: Is the Teams SBC list the same as the Azure Communication Services list
cards.def: SBC: No. They are different tables. A Teams row is not an Azure row.

cards.term: What must the voice mail pilot match
cards.def: Voice mail pilot: The route pattern that points at Unity Connection.
Advanced Features, Voice Mail, Voice Mail Pilot.
The predefined direct rule that sends a recognized user to the sign-in conversation.
Attempt Forward is the predefined forwarded rule that plays the greeting of the user whose extension forwarded the call.
Opening Greeting: No. It is always last on both routing tables.

cards.term: What do star and pound do on the Opening Greeting handler by default
cards.def: Opening Greeting: Star is sign-in. Pound is the operator.
Opening Greeting: The Undeliverable Messages distribution list.
So a forwarded call still carries the original extension. Without it, Unity often plays Opening Greeting.
Unity search space is Unity Connection's own ordered list of partitions. It is not a Unified CM calling search space.

cards.term: Multiple Tenant MWI Modes True do
cards.def: Unified CM uses translation patterns to turn voicemail extensions into directory numbers before lighting MWI.

cards.term: the UCCE 15 solutions overview print as the Unified CCE scale sentence
cards.def: UCCE: Up to 36000 multichannel agents. The reference-design chapter also describes a scale-up to 48000. Date the page you quote.
Packaged CCE's overview ceiling is up to 12000 multichannel agents. 24000 and above are Unified CCE reference designs.
SIP: Signaling. It is a B2BUA and does not touch RTP. Prompts are HTTP(S) from the voice browser.

cards.term: PGs does the UCCE-to-WxCC guide say are typically coresident
cards.def: PGs: Agent PG, VRU PG, and MR PG.

cards.term: Do UCCE scripts import into WxCC
cards.def: UCCE: No. You inventory them and recreate flows. WxCC is not a rename of the Router.

cards.term: What happens to CCX scripts in the WxCC transition guide
cards.def: CCX: They are recreated in the flow builder. Reporting moves to Analyzer.
An urgent priority is the pattern is acted on as soon as it matches, without waiting for more digits.
A line group is an ordered set of directory numbers a hunt pilot distributes. It is not a route group.
An FAC is Forced Authorization Code. A code the caller must enter before the route proceeds. It is not a CSS.
A CMC is Client Matter Code. A billing tag collected at route time. It does not choose the gateway by itself.

cards.term: GDPR in a collaboration dial plan
cards.def: A GDPR is Global Dial Plan Replication, the catalog of numbers and URIs ILS advertises. Not the privacy regulation.
Media Termination Point. It can anchor or convert media when a call needs it, including some early-offer cases.
A conference bridge is a media resource that mixes parties. It is selected from a media resource group list, not from a CSS.
Music on hold. An audio source played when a call is held. A one-way-audio hold bug can be the source or the SIP direction attributes.
The Unified CM object that sets transport and authentication for a SIP trunk, including the Unity trunk.

cards.term: a SIP profile on Unified CM
cards.def: The trunk or device object that holds SIP timers and Early Offer support for voice and video calls. Not an IOS voice class sip-profile.
Voice class sip-profiles is an IOS named set of header and SDP edits applied on the dial peer you attach it to.
A voice class server-group is more than one session target, with preference. Those addresses are trusted by default.
A voice class uri is a named match against Via, Request-URI, To, or From, used by incoming uri on a dial peer.
An incoming uri via is the first inbound SIP dial-peer test in the CUBE dial-peer guide: match the Via header.
E164-pattern-map is an outbound dial-peer tool that matches a list of E.164 numbers without one destination-pattern per number.

cards.term: media bypass in Teams Direct Routing
cards.def: A media bypass is a certification column on Microsoft's SBC page. Media can stay off the Teams media processors when the row allows it. Re-check the row.
Non-media bypass is the Direct Routing mode where media hairpins through Microsoft. The certified-SBC table marks it separately from media bypass.
A voice mail profile is the Unified CM object that points a phone or line at a voice mail pilot.
easy message access: Unity identifies the user from the calling extension so they can retrieve mail without entering an ID. A PIN may still be required.
Identified user messaging means that, on a forwarded internal call, Unity can stamp the message with the caller's extension.
An alternate extension is another number Unity treats as the user's extension for sign-in and rules. PSTN callback numbers often need one.
A call handler is a Unity object that plays a greeting and takes caller input. Opening Greeting is the default attendant.
A directory handler is a Unity object that lets a caller spell a name and transfer. It uses the Unity search space, not the line CSS.
An interview handler is a Unity object that asks a series of recorded questions. It is not an HR system.
A restriction table is Unity's allow and block list for transfers and outdials. Independent of the CUCM CSS on the trunk.
The port checkbox that lets that Unity port turn message waiting on and off.
A Unified CM device that accepts a call and hands it to a CTI application such as a contact-center peripheral.
A PIM is Peripheral Interface Manager. The PG process that speaks to one kind of device, such as Unified CM or CVP.
The process that runs scripts and selects a destination. It is not an IP router and not a CUCM route pattern.
Logger is the UCCE process that stores configuration and historical route data beside the Router.
A skill group is a collection of agents who can take a class of contact. Membership is not a calling search space.
A precision queue is UCCE routing that matches attributes on agents instead of only static skill groups.
Contact Director is a Unified CCE reference design that distributes contacts across target systems. It is not WxCC.
Survivable Remote Site Telephony. Phones register to the branch router when Unified CM is unreachable.
SRST with a richer feature set on the IOS gateway, still a WAN-failure mode and not AAR.
An MGCP gateway that drops back to local call control, often H.323 or SIP SRST, when CUCM is gone.
Phones use SIP to register to the branch router during fallback, instead of the SCCP SRST path.
An SRSV is Survivable Remote Site Voicemail. A branch Unity cache so users still reach greetings when the central Unity is unreachable.
A service profile is the Unified CM object that points Jabber or the Webex App at UC services: voicemail, directory, CTI, and IM and Presence.
A typed pointer, such as voicemail or directory, that a service profile includes.
IM and Presence subcluster is a high-availability pair of presence nodes. Users are assigned to one subcluster.
Presence and IM between organizations using SIP. It is not a CUBE dial peer by itself.
Presence federation using XMPP. Expressway or the presence node may front it. It does not route PSTN calls.
A neighbor zone is an Expressway zone to a system it can reach directly, such as Unified CM. Not the traversal pair.
Mobile and Remote Access. External clients register to Unified CM through Expressway without a VPN.
Subject Alternative Name. The Expressway-E certificate must list the collab-edge domain clients actually request.

cards.term: Deduct Audio Bandwidth from Audio Pool for Video Call
cards.def: Deduct Audio Bandwidth is the CallManager service parameter that puts a video call's audio into the audio pool. The PA example then takes 80 kbps audio and 320 kbps video from a 384 kbps call.
RAY BAUM'S Act section 506 is the dispatchable-location duty for MLTS. Fixed on-premises devices were due 6 January 2021. Non-fixed and off-premises were due 6 January 2022.
Kari's Law's install date: MLTS manufactured, imported, sold, leased, or installed after 16 February 2020 must allow direct 911 and on-site notification.
A survivability gateway is an IOS gateway that registers Webex Calling phones locally when the cloud is unreachable.
Webex Calling location is the cloud site object that holds numbers, PSTN choice, and calling permissions. It is not a Unified CM location and it does not run LBM.
A calling permission is Webex Calling's class of service: which destination classes a user may dial.

Dedicated Instance: A private-cloud Unified CM, Unity Connection, and Expressway, with IM and Presence optional and CER for the Americas. As of the Webex introduction and the DI PA retrieved 2026-10-14.

Dedicated Instance: Cisco manages infrastructure, application updates, and disaster recovery. Partners handle network capacity and customer-specific configuration. Do not delete the preconfigured multi-tenant trunks.
PreDot discard is Drop the digits before the dot, then continue analysis or prefix what remains.
Called-party transformation is a pattern applied as the call leaves, often on the gateway CSS, to make the number the carrier expects.
Dial-peer 0 is the inbound peer IOS uses when no configured peer matches. It advertises all voice codecs, enables VAD, and has no DTMF relay.
Cause 188 is Busyout when a server-group peer fails options keepalive.
The external DNS SRV that MRA clients use to find Expressway-E.
The internal DNS SRV on-premises clients use to find Unified CM.
Expedited Forwarding, decimal 46. The Collaboration 14 PA marks audio, including audio of a video call, as EF.
DSCP 34. Collaboration 14 PA marks prioritized desktop and room video as AF41.
HTTP Enabled Location Delivery. The phone asks a location server for a location URI.
Unified CM group is a prioritized list of up to three servers. First is primary, second backup, third tertiary, assigned through the device pool.

cards.term: many default routers can the phone Settings menu hold, versus the CM group
cards.def: The SRST overview says the phone menu holds at most five. Unified CM puts at most three in the group.
50 characters. Letters, numbers, period, hyphen, underscore, and space, on the Release 15 device-pool chapter.

cards.term: Who is the NTP source for subscribers
cards.def: NTP: The publisher. Subscribers and IM and Presence sync time from it.
Active media. Users cannot invoke features such as hold or transfer on that call.
Allow Peer to Preserve H.323 Calls set to True.

cards.term: What SIP response can a media change produce if the phone lost Unified CM
cards.def: Unified CM: 488 with cause 38. Do not start by editing regions.

cards.term: two things call preservation does not support.
cards.def: CTI, TAPI, and JTAPI applications, and third-party H.323 endpoints such as NetMeeting. Annunciator is on the same unsupported list.

cards.term: What are the three SRST Reference choices
cards.def: The three SRST Reference choices are Disable, Use Default Gateway, and User-Defined, under Roaming Sensitive Settings.
Connection Monitor Duration is how long the phone watches Unified CM before it leaves SRST and registers back.
SRST: Only when the phone has a single Unified CM in its list and an active standby to the router. A three-node group tries the other nodes first.

cards.term: the default keepalive on the SRST overview
cards.def: A default keepalive is 30 seconds. Discovery is typically three keepalives.
mode esrst selects Enhanced SRST, in voice register global or telephony-service.
mode Webex-sgw selects Webex Calling survivability gateway mode, in voice register global. It is not Unified CM SRST.

cards.term: does SIP SRST answer 404 every two minutes
cards.def: Phone loads 8.0 and later keepalive while still registered to Unified CM. The 404 is the keepalive answer, not a user call.

cards.term: CER know about 911 calls placed in SRST
cards.def: Nothing. After failback, PSAP callback can follow CER's default for that ELIN. Do not place a live 911 test.

cards.term: A phone is on the tertiary node. Is that SRST
cards.def: No. The tertiary node is still Unified CM. SRST is only after every node in the group is unreachable.

cards.term: May Expressway-C and Expressway-E share an IP
cards.def: Expressway-C: No. The X15.2 requirements page says shared NAT is unsupported.

cards.term: What SRV does an outside MRA client use
cards.def: _collab-edge._tls toward Expressway-E. The requirements example uses port 8443.

cards.term: What SRV does an inside client use
cards.def: _cisco-uds._tcp toward Unified CM, port 8443 in the same example.

cards.term: From X12.5, must Expressway-C resolve _cisco-uds for the external domain
cards.def: No. The client can still need the internal cisco-uds result after it reaches E.

cards.term: What inbound ports does the internal firewall need for MRA
cards.def: MRA: None, on the X15.2 requirements page. C connects outbound to E.

cards.term: the C-to-E outbound ports on that page.
cards.def: C-to-E: SIP TCP 7001, media UDP 2776-2777 or 36000-36011 when large, XMPP TCP 7400, SSH TCP 2222.
Expressway-E: SIP TCP 5061, HTTPS TCP 8443, XMPP TCP 5222, media UDP 36002-59999.

cards.term: create the traversal server zone first
cards.def: Traversal server: E listens on a specific port. The client zone has to aim at a port that already exists.

cards.term: the second SIP traversal server port if the first used 7001
cards.def: The next increment, not 7001 again. H.323 starts at UDP 6001 and increments the same way.

cards.term: is an MRA UC traversal zone built
cards.def: MRA: Encrypted SIP TLS, TLS verify on, media encryption forced. It is not the same zone as B2B.

cards.term: do generated CUCM neighbor zones include TLS
cards.def: CUCM: When Cluster Security Mode is 1, mixed mode. TCP is always generated.

cards.term: does Expressway-C's CA chain go on a non-secure CUCM
cards.def: tomcat-trust and CallManager-trust, even though the cluster is not in mixed mode.
B2B chaining is an Expressway-E can be a traversal client of another Expressway-E, as well as a traversal server for C.

cards.term: Can a VCS be the traversal peer
cards.def: VCS: No. The X15.3 traversal guide says both ends are Expressway.

cards.term: the default traversal subzone media range on C
cards.def: A default traversal subzone media range is 36000 to 59999, under Configuration, Local Zones, Traversal Subzone. Large systems reserve the first twelve ports.
GDPR means Global Dial Plan Replication. Not the European privacy regulation.
On the publisher. Advanced Features, ILS Configuration. Role is Hub Cluster or Spoke Cluster. The first cluster must be a hub.

cards.term: What checkbox turns on GDPR exchange
cards.def: GDPR: Exchange Global Dial Plan Replication Data with Remote Clusters.
The home cluster. Remote clusters need a SIP route pattern for that string, service Cisco Intercluster Lookup Service.

cards.term: Is a directory URI routable by itself
cards.def: URI: No. Local calls need its partition in the CSS. Intercluster calls use the route string.
A directory URI maximum is 254 characters after percent-encoding. joe smith#@cisco.com is 20 typed and 24 stored.
Remote clusters. You cannot use it to route a local call.

cards.term: ILS Max Number of Learned Objects in Database
cards.def: ILS Max Number of Learned Objects is the ceiling. Default 100,000 and maximum 1,000,000 on the page retrieved 2026-10-14. Lowering it below the saved count stops new writes and keeps old rows.
ILS: After database replication completes. An empty spoke during replication is not a failed hub.

cards.term: does Jabber find the home cluster without ILS
cards.def: ILS: You configure remote clusters manually, which the planning guide compares to Extension Mobility Cross Cluster.
User Management, User Settings, Service Profile. UC services are the menu beside it.

cards.term: If the service profile has no IM and Presence configuration, who authenticates
cards.def: IM: The Jabber planning chapter says the authenticator is Unified CM.

cards.term: the first check when RIS shows a phone unregistered
cards.def: A first check is DHCP, option 150, the TFTP file, and trust. Then the CM group. Not the route pattern.

cards.term: Can a learned number use a null partition
cards.def: No. The GDPR chapter says learned numbers and patterns must be in a partition, and not a null partition.
5,000 is the problem size. Not a subscriber count, not BHCA, not an Expressway maximum.
A branch is a device pool with a Unified CM group and, when the router is its own, a User-Defined SRST reference.

cards.term: not share one pool across two SRST routers
cards.def: A pool holds one SRST reference, one group, one location, and one local route group.

cards.term: does one national pattern serve every site
cards.def: Standard Local Route Group selects the gateway on the calling device's pool.

cards.term: What do you write for a location you have not measured
cards.def: Unmeasured. Do not invent a round number.

cards.term: ports does the local-gateway coexistence example use
cards.def: Ports: 5065 toward Webex Calling and 5060 toward the PSTN, on the Unified CM side.

cards.term: What must you not delete on Dedicated Instance
cards.def: The preconfigured SIP trunks between multi-tenant Webex Calling and Dedicated Instance.

cards.term: Does the CM group size tell you how many nodes to buy
cards.def: CM: No. A group holds at most three. Cluster size is a sizing-guide question this room leaves TODO-verify.

cards.term: utils network ping belongs on which node when you are proving the path
cards.def: The publisher CLI, toward the subscriber or the branch router.

cards.term: If the node returns inside the KeepAlive timer, what can the phone do
cards.def: Stay registered to the current node while the call is still in preservation. Do not teach an instant jump home.

cards.term: Single-NIC static NAT on Expressway-E is
cards.def: not recommended. If you use it, the requirements page says you need NAT reflection. Dual NIC is the design to teach.

cards.term: Large-appliance media between C and E on the requirements page is
cards.def: Large-appliance: UDP 36000 to 36011. UDP 2776 to 2777 is the other row.

cards.term: a PSTN failover number in GDPR
cards.def: PSTN failover number is an enterprise or +E.164 alternate number used when VoIP routing to the learned element fails. The remote cluster still needs a route pattern to a gateway.

cards.term: A Webex App user in Webex Calling mode
cards.def: Webex Calling: does not use this ILS path. Confirm the mode before you edit a service profile.
MRA: Expressway, not by the branch SRST reference.

cards.term: do you copy the branch pool to the other sites
cards.def: After one site is proved, including failback and, if hybrid, one Webex call. Not before.

cards.term: SIP phone loads older than 8.0 and SRST
cards.def: dual-register. Loads 8.0 and later use the two-minute keepalive.

cards.term: Authenticated SIP phones during fallback may
cards.def: SIP: fall back to TCP rather than TLS. Say so if the design requires TLS during the outage.

cards.term: Dual NIC: which name does C put in the peer field
cards.def: NIC: The FQDN of E's internal interface, not the IP, and not the public address unless split DNS and the certificate agree.

cards.term: The ILS registration popup checkbox says
cards.def: ILS: Activate the Intercluster Lookup Service on the publisher in this cluster.

cards.term: Three emergency lists in the hybrid design
cards.def: On-net from T8-R01, the CER default for SRST fallback, and the Webex emergency address with 933. Not one shared ELIN sheet.

cards.term: Disable on the SRST reference means
cards.def: phones in that pool do not try an SRST gateway.

cards.term: Search history on Expressway tells you
cards.def: which zone took the call. A partner URI on the UC traversal zone is a search-rule mistake.
is an ILS local rule checked before routing. A match means Unified CM does not route that learned string. It is not a CSS.
WAN: is not the capstone choice. It needs a round-trip figure this room will not invent.
On the publisher. Call processing runs where Cisco CallManager is active. T1-R01.

cards.term: ticket comes first, registration or the route pattern
cards.def: Route pattern: Registration. A cluster problem and a dial-plan problem are different tickets. T1-R01.

cards.term: do you read the database name, a phone count, and a registration timer
cards.def: Install guide for your SU, the Collaboration Sizing Tool, and the SIP Profile plus Cisco CallManager service parameters. Entitlements are on License Management. IdPs are in the SSO chapter. Recording method is in that feature chapter. T1-R01.

cards.term: the 12.x Preferred Architecture call the translation option that keeps the ca...
cards.def: Use Originator's Calling Search Space. That page is older than 12 months. T1-R01 does not print a Release 15 screenshot of the checkbox.

cards.term: many nodes can a Unified CM group hold
cards.def: Unified CM: At most three. The device pool is how a phone receives that list. T1-R02.

cards.term: call preservation keep, and what does it drop
cards.def: Audio stays up. Features go down. It is not the same event as a registration move. T1-R02.

cards.term: a device-level MRGL do to the device pool list
cards.def: It hides the pool list. The resource still has to be in an MRG that is in the MRGL the endpoint uses. T1-R07.

cards.term: Can the fail-call flags replace a missing transcoder
cards.def: Fail-call: No. Both flags False can let a call proceed without a software MTP or TRP. They cannot invent a codec converter. T1-R07.

cards.term: do MTP, conference, annunciator, IVR, and music on hold contend
cards.def: MTP: IPVMS is one service and one shared driver on that node. T1-R07.

cards.term: MTP translates DTMF on a secure call
cards.def: A hardware pass-through MTP from 14SU3 on IOS XE 17.10.1a, with TLS. Not IPVMS. Not H.323. Platforms named: 4461, 8200, 8300, 8000V. T1-R07.
Software MTP default of 48 is the media chapter's example for a 100-MB NIC. A 10-MB NIC example is about 24. Do not invent a VM NIC count. T1-R07.

cards.term: the annunciator default, and the dedicated-node ceiling the chapter names
cards.def: An annunciator default is 48 simultaneous streams by default. Up to 255 on a dedicated subscriber where CallManager is not running, and up to 400 if that node meets the 10,000-user OVA. T1-R07.

cards.term: What DTMF does IVR collect, and what is its default caller count
cards.def: Out-of-band DTMF only. 48 simultaneous callers by default, and the chapter says not to exceed 48 on a node. T1-R07.

cards.term: video is possible, which MTP does Unified CM prefer
cards.def: An RTCP pass-through MTP from the sponsoring endpoint's MRGL. If none exists it still inserts an MTP. An audio MTP makes the call audio-only unless IPVC is doing the work. T1-R07.

cards.term: is mixed mode typed, and where is it only read
cards.def: Typed on the publisher CLI: utils ctl set-cluster mixed-mode. Read as Cluster Security Mode value 1 under Enterprise Parameters. T1-R09.

cards.term: broken phrase on the security-modes page will you not type
cards.def: Security-modes: set utils cli. The commands are utils ctl set-cluster mixed-mode, utils ctl set-cluster non-secure-mode, and utils ctl update CTLFile. T1-R09.

cards.term: Does a non-secure cluster have an ITL
cards.def: Yes. The CTL is the mixed-mode file. A phone that already has a CTL uses it to judge the next ITL. T1-R09.

cards.term: LSC or MIC for secure mode, and what do you delete before moving a secure phone
cards.def: LSC takes precedence over MIC. Delete the old LSC, because the other cluster's CAPF is not in the CTL, and delete the CTL. T1-R09.

cards.term: page says a 90-day evaluation cannot carry a secure SIP trunk
cards.def: 90-day: The Configure Trunks restrictions table, not the mixed-mode procedure. The token still needs Allow export-controlled functionality. T1-R09.

cards.term: the install state of CDR and CMR
cards.def: CDR on, CMR off. Call Diagnostics Enabled defaults to Disabled. T1-R10.

cards.term: a leading underscore on a CDR filename mean
cards.def: leading underscore means the file is still being written. The agent sends it only after that character is gone. T1-R10.

cards.term: many billing servers can the CDR repository push to
cards.def: CDR: Up to three, by FTP or SFTP. A file that was not delivered is left in place and an alarm is raised. T1-R10.

cards.term: Is there a class-of-service object on Unified CM
cards.def: No. Class of service is a partition plus a calling search space. T2-R01.

cards.term: do emergency patterns belong in the chapter's example
cards.def: On the device, in Base_CSS. Toll privilege belongs on the directory number. T2-R01 and T1-R01.

cards.term: A partition is full of patterns and still unreachable. Why
cards.def: No calling search space the caller uses contains it. T2-R01.

cards.term: What should a route pattern point at
cards.def: Route pattern: A route list. A gateway used directly cannot also sit in a route group. T2-R02.

cards.term: the route list order, and what does the route group order
cards.def: The list orders groups. The group orders trunks. Local route group lets one pattern serve many sites. T2-R02.

cards.term: GDPR mean on a Unified CM dial plan
cards.def: GDPR means Global Dial Plan Replication. Not the privacy regulation. T3-R02.

cards.term: A phone never gets a TFTP file. Is that ILS
cards.def: TFTP: No. Trust, option 150, and the Unified CM group come first. T3-R02.

cards.term: What SIP trunk checkbox makes a forwarded call look like the subscriber
cards.def: SIP: Redirecting Diversion Header Delivery, inbound and outbound. T4-R01.

cards.term: A mailbox answers the wrong person. What do you check before the greeting wav
cards.def: The pilot, the profile, or the CSS. Opening Greeting is the last rule when the user is unknown, and you cannot delete it. T4-R01.

cards.term: is one SIP ladder not enough on CUBE
cards.def: A CUBE call is two SIP legs. The inbound dial peer is chosen before the outbound dial peer. T5-R01.

cards.term: the SIP URI match order to remember
cards.def: The SIP URI match order to remember is Via, then the request-URI, then To, then From. T5-R01.

cards.term: An untrusted source is dropped. Is that a codec failure
cards.def: No. With the trust list on, the source is discarded quietly. T5-R01.

cards.term: do you read a CUBE session count and the recommended IOS XE
cards.def: The platform data sheet for that train, and the Cisco software checker. Delayed-offer policy is the provider SIP guide. Cause codes, HA, and local-gateway commands are the guide for your IOS XE train. T5-R01.
Longest match, then preference, then random. huntstop ends the search. T5-R02.

cards.term: a destination dial-peer group on the inbound peer replace
cards.def: Dial-peer: The general outbound search. Prove one peer, then the next. T5-R02.

cards.term: What are the three pieces of the Unified CM trunk toward CUBE
cards.def: SIP profile, security profile, and the trunk device whose destination is CUBE. T5-R03.

cards.term: the printed destination ceiling on that trunk
cards.def: A printed destination ceiling is Sixteen. One of them can be a DNS SRV record. The chapter does not say how Unified CM picks among them. T5-R03.

cards.term: What do Best Effort and Mandatory say about an MTP
cards.def: Best Effort: no MTP is inserted. Mandatory: an MTP is inserted if needed. The detailed insertion rules are not invented in T5-R03.

cards.term: Run on All Active Unified CM Nodes change
cards.def: Run: Which cluster nodes may send the call. It does not replace the CUBE address. T5-R03.

cards.term: Is Expressway a second PBX for MRA
cards.def: PBX: No. Registration stays on Unified CM. Expressway is the traversal and the line-side path. T7-R01.

cards.term: public DNS record points at Expressway-E
cards.def: Expressway-E: _collab-edge._tls. The certificate has to match the name the client looks up. T7-R01.

cards.term: A phone fails only off premises. Which room owns it
cards.def: T7-R01, edge trust or DNS. If it also fails on the LAN, the trust file is T1-R09.

cards.term: inbound ports do X14.3 and X15.2 both print for Expressway-E
cards.def: Inbound ports: SIP TCP 5061, HTTPS 8443, XMPP 5222, and media UDP 36002 through 59999. Retrieved 2026-10-14. T7-R01.

cards.term: do you read Expressway cluster size and MRA capacity
cards.def: The capacity table for the X release you run. The scale at which MRA and business-to-business must split is the Preferred Architecture scalability section for that revision. Both move between releases. T7-R01.

cards.term: May Expressway-C and Expressway-E share one NAT address
cards.def: No. They need different addresses. A shared NAT is unsupported. T7-R03.

cards.term: DNS name is internal, and which is public
cards.def: DNS name: Internal: _cisco-uds._tcp to Unified CM. Public: _collab-edge._tls to Expressway-E. The public side must not answer cisco-uds. T7-R03 and T7-R04.

cards.term: Do MRA and business-to-business share one neighbor zone
cards.def: Business-to-business: They share the edge and still have different zones. Do not collapse them. T7-R03.

cards.term: Do registered LAN phones prove MRA
cards.def: LAN: No. They never asked for collab-edge. T7-R04.

cards.term: DNS succeeds and sign-in still fails. What Unified CM object is left
cards.def: Unified CM: A user profile that does not allow the Jabber services, or that blocks MRA for an OAuth user. T7-R04.

cards.term: many PSTN options does one Webex Calling location get
cards.def: One: Cisco Calling Plans, Cloud Connected PSTN, or a premises Local Gateway. T7-R08.

cards.term: ports separate Webex Calling from the PSTN in the coexistence example
cards.def: 5065 toward Webex Calling and 5060 toward the PSTN. The SIP trunk security profile must allow 5065. T7-R08.
Webex Edge Connect is Equinix peering of meetings and calling for guaranteed bandwidth and QoS. Not Edge for Devices, and not the Local Gateway. T7-R08.

cards.term: the Webex for Government Local Gateway column
cards.def: Webex is CUBE only, certificate-based, IOS XE 17.12.1a or later, no registration-based gateway, FIPS GCM ciphers. T7-R08.

cards.term: SRTP cipher does commercial registration-based Webex Calling support in that...
cards.def: SRTP cipher: SHA1_80 only. Do not copy that line into the government column. T7-R08.

cards.term: Kari's Law require, and from which date
cards.def: Kari's Law: 911 without a prefix, plus on-site notification, for an MLTS manufactured, imported, first sold or leased, or installed after 16 February 2020. T8-R01.

cards.term: a dispatchable location, and what were the two dates
cards.def: A dispatchable location is Validated street address plus the detail that finds the caller. Fixed on-premises automated location by 6 January 2021. Non-fixed and off-premises by 6 January 2022. T8-R01.
SRST: No. Do not place a live 911 test from this lab. T8-R01.

cards.term: do you read a civil penalty, the Kari's Law upgrade question, and ELINs per ERL
cards.def: Kari's Law: The statute and the FCC order for the case, counsel against 47 CFR 9.16, and the CER capacity section for your version. T8-R01.

cards.term: will you not say 36000 and 48000 as one UCCE number
cards.def: The 15.0(1) solutions sentence says up to 36000 multichannel agents. The reference-design chapter describes a scale-up to 48000. Webex Contact Center is not a rename. T8-R04.
5,000 is the problem size. Not a node count and not a Webex Calling limit. Centralized call processing plus SRST is the branch story. T8-R09.

cards.term: does an outbound CUBE SIP profile run
cards.def: After destination dial-peer matching, as the last step before the message leaves. CUBE does not remember or act on the edit. Content-length is recalculated. T5-R05.

cards.term: does an inbound CUBE SIP profile run
cards.def: Before regular SIP processing, so the inbound dial peer can change. It stays off until sip-profiles inbound is set under voice service voip, sip. T5-R05.

cards.term: What runs when Request-URI, Via, From, or To cannot be parsed
cards.def: Request-URI: Inbound dial-peer matching fails and the global sip-profile is applied. A profile that exists only on a dial peer never sees that request. T5-R05.

cards.term: many SIP profile copy variables can you configure
cards.def: SIP: 99. u01 through u99 are shared by inbound and outbound profiles. High availability does not checkpoint them to the standby. T5-R05.
It has to be the last rule on that header. Later rules cannot modify the short name. CUBE accepts either form and, by default, does not send compact form. T5-R05.

cards.term: SDP m-lines can a SIP profile edit
cards.def: Audio and video. Image m-lines, such as m=image with udptl t38, cannot be modified. T5-R05.

cards.term: Can you edit the default script vcs-interop in place
cards.def: Vcs-interop: No. Default scripts can be assigned to a trunk or a SIP profile and cannot be edited. Copy Contents into a new script. T5-R05.

cards.term: do you select a trunk normalization script versus a phone script
cards.def: Device, Trunk, Normalization Script for the trunk. Device, Device Settings, SIP Profile for the phone, next to SDP Transparency Profile. T5-R05.

cards.term: does SIP transparency pass a proprietary header
cards.def: When both call legs are SIP. REFER transparency lets Unified CM pass REFER without acting on it and then drop the call. T5-R05.
refer-passthrough does the default-script line says it removes Unified CM from the call because of a blind transfer between SIP trunks. T5-R05.

cards.term: the header-length limit after a SIP profile runs
cards.def: Header-length limit is the header, including its name, should not exceed 300 characters. If it does, the profile is not applied. The add value is about 220 characters. T5-R05.

cards.term: do you copy a header CUBE would otherwise drop
cards.def: CUBE: voice class sip-copylist, then voice-class sip-copylist on the incoming dial peer. The outbound profile uses peer-header sip. Contact x-cisco-tip is the pass-unsupported example. T5-R05.

cards.term: does SSO start relative to service discovery
cards.def: SSO: After the client has found Expressway-E. _collab-edge and the public cisco-uds failure stay in T7-R04. T7-R06.

cards.term: the default Authentication path after MRA is turned on
cards.def: UCM/LDAP. None is the default only until MRA is first enabled, and it is for functions that are not ordinary MRA. T7-R06.

cards.term: Who can use Authorize by OAuth token in the X14.3 access-control table
cards.def: Access-control: Cisco Jabber and Cisco Webex clients. The simple-OAuth prerequisites block still says Jabber 10.6 or later and Jabber only. Quote the section you are configuring. T7-R06.

cards.term: Who does Authorize by OAuth token with refresh add
cards.def: Authorize by OAuth token: Jabber, Webex, and Cisco IP phones that onboard with activation codes in MRA mode. Also enable OAuth with refresh on Unified CM, and on Unity Connection if Unity is used. T7-R06.

cards.term: many IdP signing certificates does MRA support
cards.def: MRA: One, for signing SAML assertions. Multiple IdP signing certificates are not supported. T7-R06.

cards.term: does an imported IdP start authenticating users
cards.def: After you associate at least one domain. One IdP per domain. One IdP can serve many domains. T7-R06.

cards.term: What Unified CM parameter must be Enabled before SIP OAuth Mode
cards.def: OAuth with Refresh Login Flow. Then add Expressway-C, run utils sipOAuth-mode enable on the publisher, restart Cisco CallManager, and check Enable OAuth Authentication on the phone security profile. T7-R06.
CEOAuth neighbor: From X12.5, Expressway names it CEOAuth plus the Unified CM name when SIP OAuth Mode is enabled. A search rule at priority 45 is created with it. T7-R06.

cards.term: What happens to secure profiles if the cluster is not mixed
cards.def: They are downgraded to use TCP. CEtls is created when Cluster Security Mode is 1, Mixed. CEtcp is the TCP neighbor. T7-R06.

cards.term: What has to be true before you export SAML metadata
cards.def: SAML: Expressway-C has a valid connection to Expressway-E. Export from the primary peer. New deployments default to one cluster-wide file. T7-R06.

cards.term: the X14.3 configuration chapter say about an AAAA record
cards.def: DNS needs a valid AAAA for Expressway-E. The MRA client returns it during the collab-edge TLS SRV query. T7-R06.

cards.term: Does SSO choose a route or replace the Expressway-E certificate
cards.def: No. Calling search spaces stay in the dial plan. The certificate is T7-R01. SSO is the identity step after the client reaches the edge. T7-R06.

cards.term: Does changing the class of service on a Unity template move existing users
cards.def: No. Editing the settings inside the class affects new and existing members. Move an existing user from Class of Services, Class of Service Membership. T4-R02.

cards.term: Unity classes of service cannot be deleted
cards.def: System and Voice Mail User COS. VoiceMailUserTemplate and AdministratorTemplate can be edited and cannot be deleted. T4-R02.

cards.term: does an administrator who needs voice mail get two accounts
cards.def: One account has no mailbox and signs in to Administration. The other has a mailbox and sends and receives messages. T4-R02.

cards.term: the private-list cap the Unity chapter prints
cards.def: Private-list cap the Unity chapter prints is the class sets the maximum, up to 99. The worked case allows 15. The phone ignores empty lists. The Messaging Assistant counts a named empty list. T4-R02.

cards.term: Can you edit a Unity system role
cards.def: No. System roles cannot be created, modified, or deleted. Only a System Administrator can assign them. Help Desk Administrator resets passwords and PINs, unlocks accounts, and views settings. T4-R02.

cards.term: What are the Based on Template values on the New User page
cards.def: Based is VoiceMailUserTemplate and AdministratorTemplate. The add-user procedure does not apply to Business Edition end users. T4-R02.

cards.term: Who can delete the install Administrator account
cards.def: Only after the System Administrator role sits on at least one other user. Operator, Undeliverable Messages Mailbox, and Unity Connection Messaging System cannot be deleted. T4-R02.

cards.term: Is a Unity class of service a Unified CM calling search space
cards.def: No. It limits mailbox features for members of that class. The membership page is Class of Services, plural. T4-R02.

cards.term: pre-upgrade version can use a clusterwide direct standard upgrade to Release 15
cards.def: Pre-upgrade version: 12.5(1) or later. Software Upgrades, Install/Upgrade Cluster is hidden when From is pre-12.5(1). The publisher CLI is utils system upgrade cluster. T8-R10.

cards.term: Is there a direct refresh from pre-12.5.x to Release 15
cards.def: No. 10.5, 11.0, 11.5, and 12.0 use a PCD 15 migration or a fresh install with data import. T8-R10.
Switch-version order is publisher inactive first. Switch and reboot the publisher before any subscriber. Wait for replication before a COP or a configuration change. T8-R10.

cards.term: UDS contact search return until every node has switched
cards.def: 503 Service Unavailable. That hits newly signed-in Jabber clients and desk phones that use UDS. T8-R10.
14SU4: 15SU2 or higher. 15 and 15SU1a are not a valid option. The planning table names CSCwi85184. T8-R10.

The tasks chapter says it reduces the chance of a failed upgrade. The example name is ciscocm.preUpgradeCheck-00019.cop.sgn, and the latest filename may differ. It is fully supported from 10.x. T8-R10.

cards.term: is switching back to the old version unsupported
cards.def: On migrations. Most direct upgrades can switch back, and configuration made since the upgrade is lost. T8-R10.
Deprecated-phone: No additional endpoints are deprecated. 7970G, 7971G-GE, and 7921G are on the 12.0(1) row. T8-R10.
A hunt list is the prioritized list of line groups behind a hunt pilot. Enable this Hunt List must be checked or the list does not run. T2-R07.
The default Distribution Algorithm is Longest Idle Time. It offers the call only to idle members, longest idle first. T2-R07.

cards.term: Broadcast do in a line group
cards.def: Broadcast rings every idle or available member of the line group at the same time. Do not put shared-line directory numbers in that group. T2-R07.
HLog logs the phone out of every line group associated with it, because hunt group log off is device-based. T2-R07.
3200 is the combined queue-slot limit on one subscriber node, the sum of Maximum Number of Callers Allowed in Queue. T2-R07.
The default maximum wait in a hunt queue is 900 seconds, and the range is 0 to 3600 seconds. T2-R07.

cards.term: What happens when every hunt member is logged out and queuing is on
cards.def: The hunt pilot still queues calls when every member is logged out. Hunt Group Logoff Notification does not play. T2-R07.

cards.term: the broadcast directory-number recommendation with queuing
cards.def: A single line group that uses broadcast with call queuing should have no more than 35 directory numbers. T2-R07.

cards.term: the cluster hunt list device maximum
cards.def: The cluster hunt list device maximum is 15000 on one Unified CM cluster. T2-R07.
RNA Reversion Timeout is the line-group timer, in seconds, before the No Answer hunt option moves the call. The chapter does not print a default number of seconds. T2-R07.

cards.term: does Opening Greeting sit in a routing table
cards.def: Opening Greeting is always the last rule in both the direct table and the forwarded table, and it cannot be deleted. T4-R04.
A blank routing-rule field matches everything. Specify only the criteria that should select the rule. T4-R04.

cards.term: search space identifies a Unity caller before sign-in
cards.def: The routing rule's search space identifies the caller before sign-in. The user profile search space applies only after sign-in succeeds. T4-R04.

cards.term: Route from Next Call Routing Rule do on the final rule
cards.def: Route from Next Call Routing Rule applies the final rule again when the call is already on that rule. T4-R04.
Call Management > Call Routing holds Direct Routing Rules and Forwarded Routing Rules. T4-R04.

cards.term: Arbiter trace levels cover Unity call routing
cards.def: Arbiter micro trace levels 14, 15, and 16 cover call routing. Routing Rules level 11 and CDE level 4 are the companion traces. T4-R04.

cards.term: would a known user hear the Opening Greeting
cards.def: A known user hears the Opening Greeting when the calling extension is outside the Attempt Sign-In search scope, or when a different direct rule matched first. T4-R04.
A forwarded non-user extension, such as a conference room, reaches the Opening Greeting on the forwarded table. T4-R04.

cards.term: did video greetings arrive on Attempt Sign-In
cards.def: Unity Connection 10.0(1) and later can play and record video and audio greetings when the caller reaches Attempt Sign-In. T4-R04.

cards.term: What search space does cross-server sign-in need
cards.def: Cross-server sign-in needs the remote users' partitions inside the Attempt Sign-In search space on the originating server. T4-R04.
A calling party transformation pattern adapts the calling number. The chapter's example replaces an extension with the office main number. T2-R04.
A called party transformation pattern adapts the called number. The chapter's example keeps the last five digits of a ten-digit call. T2-R04.

cards.term: number selects the SIP trunk calling-party mask
cards.def: The pre-transform calling number, the extension on the IP phone, selects the SIP trunk calling-party mask even if a route pattern already changed the number. T2-R04.

cards.term: is DNA wrong about the calling party transformation mask
cards.def: DNA selects the calling party transformation mask from the transformed number. The call-routing chapter says that is the wrong behavior of DNA. T2-R04.

cards.term: Calling Party Transformation CSS of None do
cards.def: Calling Party Transformation CSS of None means the transformation does not match and is not applied. T2-R04.
The service parameter +:1 strips one digit and adds a plus, so 04423452345 becomes +4423452345. T2-R04.
The service parameter +1:6 strips six digits and leaves the prefix, so 552345 becomes +1. T2-R04.
The service parameter +1:8 strips more digits than 552345 contains, so the final calling number is blank. T2-R04.

cards.term: many digits can Calling Party Normalization strip
cards.def: Calling Party Normalization allows only 24 digits to be stripped. A strip value of :26 is rejected. T2-R04.
Clusterwide Incoming Calling Party prefixes apply only when the prefix is Default on both the device and the device pool. T2-R04.

cards.term: CSS wins for a phone roaming inside its Device Mobility Group
cards.def: The roaming device pool's Calling Party Transformation CSS wins even when Use Device Pool Calling Party Transformation CSS is unchecked. T2-R04.

cards.term: What @ expansion count does the Release 15 call-routing chapter print
cards.def: The Release 15 call-routing chapter does not print an @ expansion count. Its examples include 0, 1411, and 19725551234. It does not print 166. T2-R04.
An ordered list of partitions. Unified CM concatenates the directory-number CSS and the device CSS. The directory number CSS takes precedence.
The first Unified CM node. It owns configuration writes. Call processing usually runs on subscribers.
The default inbound dial peer IOS uses when nothing else matches. It does not carry your codec list or SIP profile.
A CUBE busyout symptom when a server-group peer fails options keepalive.
The traversal client inside the trusted network. It opens the connection toward Expressway-E.
The traversal server in the DMZ. Its public certificate must list the collab-edge discovery domain.
The external DNS SRV _collab-edge._tls that MRA clients use to find Expressway-E.
The internal DNS SRV _cisco-uds._tcp that on-premises clients use to find Unified CM.
HTTP Enabled Location Delivery. The phone asks a location server for a location URI and Unified CM can place that URI in a Geolocation header.
Expedited Forwarding, decimal 46. The Collaboration Preferred Architecture marks audio, including audio of a video call, as EF.
Assured Forwarding 41, DSCP 34. Preferred Architecture marks prioritized desktop and room-system video as AF41.
Assured Forwarding 42, DSCP 36. Preferred Architecture marks Jabber, MRA, and edge video as AF42 when the network has an opportunistic video class.
Class Selector 3, DSCP 24. Call signaling marking in the Collaboration QoS guidance.
Unified CM object that represents a LAN in Enhanced Locations CAC. Links between locations carry the bandwidth budget.
Location Bandwidth Manager. Admits or denies calls. It does not mark DSCP and it does not detect a WAN failure.
A Cisco IOS XE or third-party SBC that connects Webex Calling to premises PSTN or to Unified CM.
Not Acceptable Here. The far end rejected the SDP. Read codecs before you change the route.
show voip trace on CUBE. The debug-collection note says to prefer it before debug ccsip messages. It is on by default on recent IOS XE.
Clauses such as AREA-CODE that discard NANP patterns created by the @ wildcard.
The dot in a pattern. It marks digits to discard. It is not a dialed digit.
Stands in for NANP patterns. Use a route filter. Do not quote an unfiltered expansion count unless the page you opened prints it.
Unified CM's search of the dialed digits against the effective CSS.
Forced Authorization Code, collected before a route pattern proceeds.
Client Matter Code, a billing tag collected at route time.
A partition that is reachable only inside a time period and time schedule.
Global Dial Plan Replication. The catalog ILS advertises. Not a privacy law.
Dialed Number Analyzer. Useful, and able to pick the wrong calling-party transformation. Trust the trunk trace.
The global form of a phone number, starting with +. The Collaboration 15 PA treats it as the primary numeric address.
Default outbound order: longest match, then lower preference, then random. As of 2026-10-14.
On a dial peer, a lower number is tried first when the match length ties.
Stops outbound hunting after a failure on that dial peer.
CUBE's source check. Session targets and server groups are trusted by default. Untrusted INVITEs are silently discarded.
A named IOS object a dial peer points at: codec, URI, SIP profile, server group, or dial-peer group.
voice class sip-profiles. Header and SDP edits on one leg. Not the Unified CM SIP Profile page.
The Unified CM object that holds Early Offer support for voice and video calls.
A destination set on the inbound peer. Outbound matching stays inside it.
voice class server-group. Several session targets. Their addresses are trusted.
Prints SIP on a CUBE. Use it after VoIP trace and turn it off.
The number users dial, and the number forwards use, to reach Unity. It must match the route pattern.
Points a phone or a line at a voice mail pilot. The pilot number and the route pattern must match, or the Messages button goes nowhere.
Unity's predefined direct rule. Recognized users go to sign-in.
Unity's predefined forwarded rule. The forwarding extension selects the greeting.
Unity's last routing rule and the default automated attendant. It cannot be deleted.
An ordered list of Unity partitions. Not a Unified CM calling search space.
Unity's allow and block list for transfers. Independent of the CUCM CSS.
A second number Unity treats as the user, for sign-in or forwarded calls.
A Unity greeting plus caller input. Opening Greeting is one.
A Unity object that looks up a user by name. It is not the opening greeting and it is not a Unified CM directory URI.
A Unity object that asks a sequence of questions.
Voice Profile for Internet Mail. How Unity systems exchange messages with other voicemail systems.
Voicemail delivered into an email mailbox. Sizing limits stay on the design guide.
The script engine that selects an agent or a treatment. Not an IP router.
The UCCE edge that faces Unified CM, CVP, or a multichannel source.
Webex Contact Center. A cloud contact center. Not a rename of UCCE or UCCX.
A Unified CCE reference design that sends contacts to other systems.
Unified Contact Center Express. The smaller on-premises product beside Unified CM.
Packaged Contact Center Enterprise. A bounded Unified CCE reference design, up to 12000 agents in the 15.0(1) overview sentence.
Survivable Remote Site Telephony. Branch registration when Unified CM is unreachable.
A richer SRST feature set on the branch router. Still a WAN-failure mode.
The gateway leaves CUCM MGCP control and runs local call processing.
Survivable Remote Site Voicemail. Unity Connection's branch survivability, distinct from router SRST. The port and mailbox caps stay TODO-verify.
Points a client at UC services: voicemail, directory, CTI, presence.
One typed destination inside a service profile: voicemail, directory, conferencing, or IM and Presence. The profile is what Jabber retrieves after it finds the home cluster.
A high-availability pair of IM and Presence nodes. Users are assigned to a subcluster. It is not a Unified CM group.
Presence and instant messaging with another organization over SIP. It is not a SIP trunk for phone calls, and it is not Global Dial Plan Replication.
Presence and instant messaging with another organization over XMPP. Expressway can carry the XMPP traversal for MRA on TCP 7400 in the X15.2 firewall list.
The Expressway zone pair that crosses a firewall. Expressway-C is the traversal client. Expressway-E is the traversal server. MRA uses a Unified Communications traversal zone.
An Expressway zone to a directly reachable system such as Unified CM.
Mobile and Remote Access through Cisco Expressway. An external client finds Expressway-E with _collab-edge._tls, then Expressway-C reaches Unified CM.
Subject Alternative Name on a certificate. Expressway-E must list the collab-edge domain.

The audio a held party hears. The source is chosen through the media resource group list. SIP SRST's own overview says music on hold is not supported for a hold invoked from a SIP phone on the releases that table lists.
The default Unified CM location. Devices there do not deduct link bandwidth.
The bandwidth budget between two Unified CM locations. Weight picks the path. LBM does not follow OSPF.
Deduct Audio Bandwidth from Audio Pool for Video Call. Keeps EF audio in the audio pool.
80 kbps in the Collaboration 14 PA example: 64 kbps payload plus 16 kbps IP and UDP.
Cisco Emergency Responder. Tracks phones to ERLs and ELINs. On Dedicated Instance the introduction limits CER to the Americas.
A location provider Webex Calling and Unified CM can use for emergency location.
Webex Calling's class of service. It does not import Unified CM calling search spaces. T8-R06 is the migration room.
A cloud site: numbers, PSTN, and permissions. Not a Unified CM location.
A Webex Calling PSTN option where Cisco is the carrier.
Webex Calling uses your trunks through a local gateway.
Microsoft's own PSTN attachment for Teams Phone. Not Direct Routing.
The SRST habit of limiting what a branch phone may dial while survived.
SIP OPTIONS between CUBE and a server-group target. Failure can busy the target out with cause 188.
Session Description Protocol. Codecs, ports, and direction. A 488 means the far end rejected it.
The UCCE server administrators and historical reporting use beside the Logger.
A tested UCCE shape with a published agent scale, such as 2000 or 4000. Exceeding it means pick a larger design, not a blog number.
The Release 15 license transport. From 15SU2 the preferred transport taught in T1-R01 is Smart Transport.
The ordered subscribers a device pool uses for registration.
CUCM invites a recorder from the built-in bridge or from a gateway forking session.
CUBE copies RTP toward a recorder. It changes SDP and can look like one-way audio.
Encrypted RTP. It requires a key exchange the trunks actually allow.
Encrypted SIP. A trust-list drop is not an expired certificate, and an expired certificate is not a CSS miss.
CUBE high availability between two routers. The procedure stays on the HA guide for the IOS XE you run.
An extra named local route group beyond Standard Local Route Group, still mapped on the device pool.
The calling or called party transformation CSS. It is not the line CSS and it is not consulted the same way.
The instruction on a pattern: PreDot, or a fixed number of leading digits.
Digits added after discard, such as + on a globalization translation.
A translation or route pattern whose route option is Block, used to reject a class of calls inside a CSS.
The CSS used when a phone forwards. It can be narrower or wider than the line CSS. A forward to voicemail still needs the pilot.
The multitenant example in the Unity SIP guide: 972813XXXX beside 214333XXXX.
The distribution list that receives messages left in the Opening Greeting handler.
A user dials another Unity server's pilot and is identified only if the search space at Attempt Sign-In includes them.
The key the Router uses to pick a script. It is the number after your translations, not the number the caller thinks they dialed.
UCCE has selected the agent and is delivering the call. A silent phone is then a device or PG problem.
Expanded call context. Data the script attaches for the desktop. WxCC desktops do not inherit it automatically.
A proxy between the gateway and CVP so more than one CVP can take the call.
The CVP flow reference designs support: treatment, queue, and transfer to an agent.
A contact-center shape outside the published reference designs, including some Unified IP IVR deployments. Limits change.
An older JTAPI treatment option discussed with non-reference designs. Not the reference-design queue.
An agent who takes calls on a PSTN phone. It has its own PG capacity notes in the design guide.
UCCE predictive or progressive dialing. SIP from the dialer has its own transport rules in the design guide.
The inbound rate a reference design is sized for. Do not invent a CPS figure for a proposal.
A Dedicated Instance subscriber at the customer site that takes registrations when the path to the cloud cluster fails.
Session Management Edition. A Unified CM cluster that aggregates trunks. Dedicated Instance offers it when enough clusters exist.
The SIP trunks Cisco builds between multi-tenant Webex Calling and Dedicated Instance. The PA says not to delete them.
Dedicated Instance operations: Cisco runs infrastructure and disaster recovery. Partners run customer-specific configuration and network capacity.
Disaster Recovery System. On Dedicated Instance, Cisco takes the backups and partners do not get the archive as a change-backout tool.
