The public DNS record _collab-edge._tls. The X15.2 MRA requirements chapter shows it aimed at Expressway-E on port 8443.
The internal DNS record _cisco-uds._tcp. The X15.2 chapter shows it aimed at Unified CM on port 8443 so on-premises clients can find the cluster.
Expressway-C. It opens the firewall traversal connection toward Expressway-E. No inbound ports are required on the internal firewall in the X15.2 requirements chapter.
Expressway-E in the DMZ. It holds the public certificate and accepts the traversal connection that Expressway-C opens.
Token renewal for clients that do not rely on a CTL. Confirm which mode the client uses before a mixed-mode change.
Business-to-business calling through Expressway, separate from MRA unless you are under the scale limit the PA tells you to check.
A cloud connector for directory, calendar, or serviceability. It is not a Local Gateway trunk, not Webex Edge Connect, and not Expressway-E.
Synchronizes users into Control Hub. SSO for synchronized users comes after that sync, per the CCX transition guide's identity note.
The older UC client. Service profiles and MRA still apply when it is the client you support.
Availability state published by IM and Presence. It does not light a voicemail lamp.
Who may see a user's presence. Not a calling search space.
IM rooms that keep history on the presence servers.
A copy of instant messages for retention. Separate from voice recording.
Presence can show in-a-meeting from a calendar. A broken calendar does not break the dial plan.
The name that must appear on certificates when Expressway is clustered. A SAN miss looks like an intermittent MRA failure.
The licensing transport preferred from Unified CM 15SU2, as taught in T1-R01.
The older Smart Licensing transport. Not the preferred one on a current 15SU if T1-R01's reading still holds. Re-check the licensing guide.
The defaults a new mailbox inherits, including class of service and the conversation.
What a mailbox owner may do: transfers, IMAP, and similar. Not the CUCM line CSS.
A Unity dial-plan container. A user outside the conversation's search space is unidentified.
The Unity object that represents one integrated PBX, with ports. The SIP guide's multiple-phone-system cap is in a different guide.
The Unity SIP ports toward Unified CM, including which ports send MWI.
A client view of messages. It still needs the pilot and the mailbox. It is not MWI.
Unity's transcription option. A later feature. It does not choose the routing rule.
Unity's multitenant mode, paired with the CUCM masks and MWI translations in the SIP guide.
The CUCM service parameter that applies translations before lighting a lamp.
An ISDN protocol for features such as MWI between PBXs. The Unity chapter points MWI relay at the CUCM docs.
Intercluster trunk. MWI relay across it is a CUCM feature, not a Unity port setting.
A SIP trunk into a Session Management Edition cluster so leaf clusters share a dial plan.
A Unified CM SIP script that edits headers on a trunk. Different tool from an IOS SIP profile, same class of accident.
The language of a Unified CM SIP normalization script on a SIP trunk. It is not a CUBE SIP profile. Do not paste a header rewrite you have not tested on that trunk.
The SIP Profile value that sends SDP when Unified CM already knows the caller's media, without forcing an MTP.
The SIP Profile value that inserts an MTP when Unified CM must send an offer and does not yet have SDP.
Voice activity detection. Dial-peer 0 enables it. Explicit peers should say whether you want it.
How digits are carried after the call connects, often RFC 2833 or SIP KPML. Dial-peer 0 does not relay them.
Telephone events in RTP. The DTMF method many providers require.
The order inside a voice class codec. The intersection with the far end is the offer/answer result.
SIP Not Acceptable Here. Read the SDP before you change a route.
SIP Not Found. Often a dial-plan miss, not a codec miss.
SIP Service Unavailable. On CUBE, look for a peer that was busy-out or a trust drop you mistook for a carrier failure.
The Q.850 code inside a SIP message. CUBE may map it. Do not assume the code is preserved.
P-Asserted-Identity. A calling-number header. The provider may want it instead of From.
The SIP URI that is the called number on that leg. After a translation, this is the number the next hop matches.
Re-INVITE or UPDATE for hold, transfer, or codec change. Blocked mid-call signaling looks like one-way audio after hold.
The interface a dial peer uses as the SIP source. The right peer on the wrong interface fails the trust list on the far side.
Where an outbound dial peer sends the call. That address is trusted for inbound connections.
An inbound dial-peer match on the called number, after the URI tests.
An inbound match on the calling number. Later than URI and called-number tests.
The outbound, and last-resort inbound, digit pattern on a dial peer.
A dial-peer tag used when more than one carrier could match. It is a later inbound test.
COR lists on dial peers. IOS class of restriction at the branch. Not a CUCM CSS.
An IOS voice translation-profile. It edits numbers on a dial peer. Not a CUCM translation pattern, though the job is similar.
A single IOS rule inside a profile. Test it with test voice translation-rule before you attach it.
How many directory numbers SRST will host. A number larger than the license or the platform is a lab fiction.
How many SCCP phones SRST will accept. SIP SRST uses a different knob.
An SRST command that maps a pilot to a local extension while survived, so the hunt still lands somewhere.
The CUCM forward used when the phone is not registered, which is the WAN-down case SRST also covers. AAR does not do this.
Call Forward Unregistered. Where a directory number goes when the phone is not registered to Unified CM. It is a different path from SRST, which is the phone registering somewhere else.
Call Forward No Answer. The PA's bandwidth-denial note mentions this field. Re-check the Release 15 AAR interaction before you build from that sentence alone.
A codec some clients offer. If it is not in the region or the voice class, the call will not use it, no matter what the phone prefers.
A wideband codec used by soft clients. Regions and CUBE voice classes have to allow it or the offer is theater.
64 kbps wideband. The PA deducts it like G.711: 80 kbps with IP and UDP overhead.
8 kbps payload in the PA narrative. Add overhead the same way only as a labeled estimate until you re-read that row.
The location-link budget for video. Separate from audio when deduct-audio is true.
The location-link budget for audio, including video-call audio when the service parameter says so.
How much of a WAN you give the priority queue. The PA does not print one percent for every circuit.
The provider's rate limit. Size the queue under it, and the CAC pool under the queue.
The on-site party who must learn about a 911 call. A route pattern does not page them by itself.
CER learns which phone is in which ERL from switch CAM or similar data. Moving a phone without tracking moves the callback address.
RAY BAUM'S Act duty for soft clients that are not at a tracked switch port. Due 6 January 2022 for that class.
The NANP piece a route filter can test, alongside area code.
011 in the NANP, often translated to + after PreDot.
A leading 9 or 8 that selects a route and is discarded before the carrier sees it.
A call that enters at one site and leaves the PSTN at another to save tolls. Locations CAC and the route list both have to allow it on purpose.
A cluster-wide or per-server CUCM knob, such as Multiple Tenant MWI Modes or the deduct-audio flag.
A cluster-wide setting that is not a per-service parameter.
Cisco's older security architecture name. Do not treat a slide titled SAFE as the current CUBE hardening guide.
The CUBE check that is on by default in the hardening guide. Leave it on.
What CUBE does with an untrusted INVITE unless you change it. A response tells a scanner that SIP is open.
A session target learned from an up dial peer. It disappears when the peer is shut or marked down.
An address you configured under ip address trusted list. It survives a peer shutdown.
The first key of dial-peer hunt 0, and also how CUCM prefers a more specific pattern over a wild one.
The wait after ! or a pattern that is a prefix of a longer pattern. Urgent 911 skips it.
A longer explicit match beats a wildcard. The route-pattern lab breaks ties toward the pattern you listed first, and says so.
A forwarding label this lab has not re-confirmed on the Release 15 page. Leave it TODO-verify rather than teaching a 12.x caption.
An override some admins remember on the route group. This lab has not confirmed the Release 15 label. TODO-verify.
A route-list member resolved from the calling device pool, so one pattern serves many sites.
The device CSS that remains when an Extension Mobility user logs out. Put 911 there.
Extension Mobility. A user logs into a phone and receives a device profile (lines, CSS, services). Logout should leave an emergency-capable profile behind.
Single Number Reach. A remote destination rings with the desk. It is not a contact-center skill.
A mobile number associated with a user for SNR or similar features.
iDivert sends a ringing or held call to voicemail. It uses the voicemail profile.
Immediate divert of a ringing or connected call to the voice mail pilot. It still needs a CSS that can reach the pilot.
CUCM can retry a busy extension later. It is not PSAP callback, and it is not MWI.
A call is held on a park number anyone in the CSS can retrieve. The park range is a pattern.
A user answers a ringing phone in the same pickup group. The CSS still has to reach that group.
The shared-line setting that blocks barge. Not a presence privacy list.
The caller hears MoH or silence. SDP direction changes. A SIP profile can 'fix' hold into one-way audio.
A new leg. The CSS of the transferrer has to reach the target. Contact-center transfers also hit the script.
Three or more parties. Fails when the media resource group list has no bridge, which looks nothing like a CSS miss except that the call cannot complete.
A conference the user builds with the conference key, as opposed to Meet-Me.
Stops the camera. It is not a location bandwidth change. CAC already deducted.
A LAN in Enhanced Locations CAC. Not a Webex Calling location.
The CUCM model of locations and links. AAR is the optional PSTN reroute when this model says no.
Phones unregister or fail over to SRST. AAR will not fire, because AAR is for a CAC denial while the cluster is reachable.
Phones leaving SRST and registering to CUCM again. A clean failback is a test, not a hope.
How fast a phone notices CUCM is gone. The default belongs to the phone firmware guide, not a guess.
The file phones download in mixed mode. A bad one looks like a registration failure after a certificate change.
Initial Trust List. Phones use it to trust CUCM. Deleting it is a recovery step, not a dial-plan step.
The CUCM web and several service identities. Renewing it without a plan strands phones and applications.
The certificate phones use for secure signaling. It belongs in the trust story, not in a route pattern.
One certificate with several names. Expressway-E clustering needs the names clients dial, not every internal hostname you own.
Certificate signing request. The names on the CSR are the names you will be stuck with.
The issuer between the server certificate and the root. The cert-chain lab checks that this link exists. It does not check the signature math.
The trust anchor. Phones and Expressway need it in the right store, not only on your laptop.
An issuer the internet already trusts. Expressway-E wants one. Unified CM usually does not use a public cert for phones.
An issuer you run. Fine inside the enterprise. Not a substitute for the Expressway-E public name.
MRA from outside fails at TLS while on-premises phones can still be fine. Check the date before the dial plan.
The Expressway name that must be on the certificate if clients use it.
Expressway-E with an inside and a DMZ interface. The traversal path and the firewall rules follow that choice.
Traversal Using Relays around NAT. Media relay on Expressway when the direct path fails.
Interactive Connectivity Establishment. Clients try direct media before a relay.
TLS SIP toward Expressway-E, in the X15.2 requirements this lab cited.
A port the MRA requirements page lists toward Expressway. IM failure with working calls often lands here.
One of the inbound ports the MRA requirements page lists for Expressway.
Single sign-on. It does not replace the Expressway-E certificate and it does not choose a route.
Identity provider for SSO. The matrix of which IdP works with which UC version stays TODO-verify.
The protocol most UC SSO deployments use. A SAML failure is an identity failure, not a codec failure.
Token-based client auth. Read the MRA guide section for the client you ship before you schedule mixed mode.
What a Webex App on MRA can extend so users are not prompted constantly. The X15.0 overview points at that section.
Webex App registered to Unified CM. Uses MRA when it is outside.
The client is a cloud calling client. It does not use the collab-edge path this room describes.
Routing between locations and trunks in Control Hub. Partitions do not import.
A Webex Calling egress set. The migration room notes it does not live inside a location the way a CUCM device does.
The cloud trunk aimed at a local gateway. In the coexistence guide this lab uses, Unified CM uses port 5065 toward Webex Calling.
The coexistence example for Unified CM toward the Webex Calling side of a local gateway, with 5060 toward the PSTN.
The usual SIP UDP or TCP port. In the coexistence example it is the PSTN side, not every call.
The colocation article this lab cited allows a survivability gateway on the same Cisco IOS box as a local gateway, and not on a third-party SBC.
May be a local gateway if Webex supports it. The colocation article said it does not host survivability. Host that separately.
Moving everyone in one window. The UCCE-to-WxCC guide allows it and also allows phased migration.
Moving queues or sites across windows, with a written rollback.
A claim this lab does not make. The transition guides list what changes. They do not say every gadget survives.
A Finesse UI extension. The WxCC guide tells you to note gadgets that have no supported equivalent.
The older agent desktop name. Current on-premises desktops in this lab's guides are Finesse.
An older desktop integration. Do not describe a new build as CTI OS.
The historic name for the UCCE routing software. People still say ICM script.
The device world a PG faces: Unified CM, CVP, or a multichannel server.
How UCCE decides which agent device to use when the agent has more than one. A wrong rule rings the wrong phone.
The comprehensive CVP network VRU type the design guide discusses for reference-style flows.
A small CVP instruction from the script, such as a prompt. Call Studio applications are the larger alternative.
The tool that builds CVP VXML applications. Those applications are part of the inventory before a WxCC move.
Voice XML. What the browser executes. Fetched over HTTP(S), not carried as the SIP body of the queue.
One of the SIP legs a contact-center proxy may see besides the caller, the browser, and the agent. The design guide's proxy note counts them.
A prompt played to the agent before they connect. Same sizing caution as agent greeting.
The supervisor hears the agent. It needs a monitoring path the desktop and the phone both support.
A supervisor joins the call. Different feature from shared-line barge, same English word.
Where a contact waits. In UCCE that wait is CVP treatment. In WxCC it is a cloud queue. The word survives. The platform does not.
What an agent can do. UCCX, UCCE skill groups, and precision queues are three implementations.
Contact Service Queue. The UCCX name for a queue. It does not exist as a CSQ inside UCCE.
The UCCX script trigger. A different object from a CUCM application user, which is a CTI credential.
A CUCM user that applications use for CTI. The contact center's PG uses one. It is not a human agent.
A human in CUCM. Agents are end users with device associations.
Which phones a user controls. Extension Mobility and CTI both care.
Unified CM administration rights. It decides which admin menus a user may open. It is not a calling search space.
A bundle of CUCM admin permissions inside an access control group.
A common CUCM access control group. Membership is an admin decision, not a dial-plan decision.
Lockout and expiry for CUCM and Unity passwords. A locked mailbox looks like a greeting failure if you do not check it.
The phone password for Unity sign-in and for Extension Mobility. They are not the same PIN unless you synchronized them.
Unity's name for the dialogue a caller or a subscriber hears, such as the sign-in conversation.
The keypad dialogue. A speech conversation is a different assignment.
The prompt a handler or a user plays. Standard, alternate, busy, and closed are different greetings.
Plays outside the schedule. If every caller hears it at noon, the schedule is wrong.
An override greeting, often used for a holiday. It wins over the standard greeting while it is enabled.
Unity's time condition for greetings and transfer rules. Independent of CUCM time-of-day partitions.
Unity can take a message or transfer to a phone. The transfer uses the restriction table and then CUCM.
Unity's transfer behavior during open hours. A greeting that cannot dial a number the phone can dial is often the restriction table, not the route pattern.
The key map on a handler. Star and pound on Opening Greeting default to sign-in and operator.
The handler pound reaches by default from Opening Greeting.
Unity recipients of a message. Opening Greeting messages go to the Undeliverable Messages distribution list. If that list is empty, nobody hears them.
How long Unity keeps a message. A compliance question, not a routing question.
A Unity list you address by extension. That extension still has to be reachable in the Unity search space.
Digital networking between Unity servers. Cross-server sign-in depends on search spaces.
Unity networking sites. Not CUCM locations and not Webex Calling locations.
The Unity search space applied to a call at a given step. Attempt Sign-In uses the one in force at that step.
A Unity rule for calls dialed straight to the voicemail pilot. The predefined direct rules are Attempt Sign-In, then Opening Greeting.
A Unity rule for calls the phone system redirected. The predefined forwarded rules are Attempt Forward, then Opening Greeting.
The CUCM CSS on the Unity trunk for calls Unity transfers back out. Empty means those transfers fail.
The CSS CUCM uses for some feature invocations. Confirm the feature's own page before you assume it is the line CSS.
The CSS a phone uses for presence subscriptions to directory numbers. A presence 'unknown' can be this CSS, not the presence service.
Busy lamp field. A speed dial that shows state. It needs the SUBSCRIBE CSS.
Speed dial plus presence. Two different failures: the call and the lamp.
Park aimed at a specific park number. Retrieve it by dialing that number. It is not a hunt pilot and it is not hold.
A one-way or two-way line that whispers into another phone. It has its own CSS pair.
The CSS an intercom line uses. It is not the normal line CSS.
The phone forks the media for recording. Off-premises phones may not be able to do this. The recording method itself stays TODO-verify.
The SBC or the voice gateway forks media. CUBE forking is the T5 topic.
Cisco Unified Border Element. The IOS XE SBC this lab configures in T5.
Session border controller. CUBE is Cisco's. Teams Direct Routing requires one on Microsoft's list.
Integrated Services Router. Several CUBE platforms on the Teams list, as of 2026-10-14, are ISR families.
An edge platform family on Microsoft's CUBE rows as of 2026-10-14. Confirm the exact model on the page.
A CUBE platform on the Teams list as of 2026-10-14.
The virtual router row on the Teams CUBE list as of 2026-10-14.
The software train CUBE runs. Certification is a row on Microsoft's page, not a number frozen in this lab.
A CUBE guide train this lab cites for dial-peer groups and SIP profiles, and the train Cisco's Direct Routing note tested. Not automatically the row Microsoft lists this week.
The quick view of tags, preferences, and whether a peer is up.
The CUBE command that lists static trusted addresses and the dynamic ones learned from session targets and server groups.
The IOS command that selects scheme 0 through 7. If it is absent, you are on the default, scheme 0.
Dial-peer hunt 0, from the IOS and IOS XE call-routing note retrieved 2026-10-14: longest match, then lower preference, then random.
One of the alternate hunt schemes, 1 through 7. Do not describe it unless the router shows that scheme.
The inbound dial-peer command that matches a voice class uri.
A SIP proxy a dial peer can target instead of the carrier directly. Contact-center designs often place one in front of CVP.
Not an Expressway zone. People mix the words. On CUBE you have dial peers and interfaces.
A neighbor, traversal, DNS, or ENUM zone. Search rules live here.
Expressway's ordered match that sends a call to a zone. It is not a CUCM CSS, though interviews compare them.
An Expressway rewrite of a called or calling URI before the search rule.
An Expressway zone that looks up the far domain. Business-to-business uses it.
Mapping phone numbers to URIs. An Expressway zone type, and a dial-plan idea.
Call processing language on Expressway. Policy scripts. Easy to forget while chasing certificates.
A CUCM or trunk setting that refuses non-TLS or non-SRTP. A lab that 'stopped working' after security was turned on is often this.
A TLS misconfiguration. The hardening guides tell you not to allow it. This lab does not paste cipher strings it has not re-read.
CUCM security mode that issues a CTL. Confirm OAuth clients before you enable it.
CUCM without the CTL requirement. Phones still have an ITL.
A way to run mixed mode without the hardware tokens. Confirm the security guide for the version you run.
The list the WxCC transition guide asks for before design: users, skills, scripts, numbers, gadgets.
The lifecycle the UCCE-to-WxCC guide uses: prepare, plan, design, implement, operate.
Running two systems while users move. Webex Calling coexistence uses the local gateway. Contact-center coexistence is a different plan.
Numbers and features that will not move in a calling migration. Write it down. CSS names are on it.
Phones or endpoints a migration flow should skip. The exact list for a given tool stays TODO-verify.
Users on both systems during a calling migration. Trunk sizing for that period is TODO-verify against the customer's traffic, not a default in this lab.
Emergency addresses and ELINs are recreated on the Webex side. CER switch ports do not import.
An emergency call that reaches the wrong site or a queue. A route pattern that completes is not compliance.
The location is specific enough for a responder. A street address without a floor can fail that test inside a tower.
Not always 911. This lab does not invent the number for a country it has not cited.
Section 506. Dispatchable location. Fixed on-premises by 6 January 2021. Non-fixed and off-premises by 6 January 2022.
The rule that carries the RAY BAUM'S Act MLTS location duties. Penalty amounts stay TODO-verify.
Not printed in this lab. The statute pages move. Look up the current figure the week you cite it.
How many people a contact center is sized for. Use the reference-design row, dated, not a round number from a meeting.
The figure in the UCCE 15.0(1) solutions sentence for Unified CCE. Re-check beside the 48000 scale-up section before a proposal.
The Packaged CCE figure in that same solutions sentence.
A further scale-up the 15.0(1) reference-design chapter describes. Not the number to quote from the solutions sentence.
The smallest named Unified CCE reference design in the 15.0(1) chapter.
A named reference design. If you need more reporting users than the 2000 model allows, the limits chapter tells you to move up.
The virtual machine template. Contact-center scale-up changes OVA sizes. Do not copy RAM figures from memory.
Agent, VRU, and MR PG on one VM, which the transition guide calls the standard layout.
One half of a redundant UCCE pair. Calls can survive on the other side.
The other half. Know which side is active before you reboot anything.
The UCCE network users and peripherals use. The HA chapter treats public and private failures differently.
How UCCE routers decide they are allowed to become active. Do not improvise a failover.
Contact-center and CUCM both assume synchronized clocks. Certificate validity and logs depend on it.
A record that returns several targets. CUBE and CUCM trunks can use it. The exact command stays on the guide for your release.
A trunk destination that depends on DNS. A failed lookup looks like a down trunk.
A local-gateway attachment that uses a certificate instead of a registration. Confirm the current LGW guide.
A local gateway that registers to Webex Calling, as opposed to a gateway that only receives calls on a trunk. T8-R06 names both.
The Control Hub tenant. Dedicated Instance is an add-on to a Webex Calling subscription, not a separate product you invent numbers for.
What was purchased. Features you did not buy are not 'missing configuration.'
A Dedicated Instance geography, such as Americas or EMEA. Customers order the regions they need. Not a CUCM region.
DI subscribers in more than one data center in a region. Enhanced Survivability is the additional site-level node.
The operator of customer-specific DI configuration, per the PA retrieved 2026-10-14.
Cisco support. A missing CSS is not a TAC outage. A down data center is.
When you apply a dial plan or a cut. Write the rollback in the same window.
A trace, a DNA result, or a show command. A feeling that the CSS is wrong is not evidence.
The CUCM SDL or SIP trace of the egress leg. It beats DNA for calling-party transformations.
System Diagnostic Layer. CUCM's detailed trace. Collect it for a window, not for a week.
Real-Time Monitoring Tool. How you pull SDL and phone logs without living on the console. It is not a substitute for a CUBE VoIP trace.
Unity's diagnostic flags. The troubleshooting guide names Arbiter, Routing Rules, and CDE for a sign-in that hits Opening Greeting.
Unity levels 14 through 16 for call routing, per the Release 15 troubleshooting guide.
Unity level 4 for search space, in that same troubleshooting note.
Whether a Unity port is idle, answering, or sending MWI. A full port group is a busy condition, not a CSS miss.
How many calls Unity will answer. The number belongs to the license and the design guide, not this page.
When a box is full, callers may not leave mail. That is not a routing-rule failure.
A message fanned out inside Unity. Failure here is messaging, not the SIP trunk.
TLS to Unity, with certificates the integration guide's next-generation section describes. This room does not paste cipher lists.
The Unity SIP guide's section for stronger TLS and SRTP. Turn it on only when both sides match.
The CUCM trunk checkbox the Unity integration procedure mentions when you encrypt.
What Unity puts in the Contact header: DN, URI, or both. The integration guide lists the three choices.
Unity's default connected-party setting in the SIP integration procedure.
Unity and CUCM on one server. The SIP integration guide says it does not apply to that layout.
A separate Unity server or cluster, which is the layout the SIP guide configures.
More than one Unity node. The integration tasks include cluster mode. This lab does not copy the node cap.
The first Unity node, same idea as CUCM: configuration lives there.
An additional Unity node. Ports can be spread across nodes.
A call-processing node. Phones register here. The publisher can be down and calls continue.
The first Unified CM node. Configuration writes go here. Subscribers sync time from it. The ILS service this lab cites runs on the publisher.
The CUCM service that processes calls. A subscriber without it does not host phones.
Serves phone files. Usually on more than one node.
The CUCM service JTAPI and some desktops connect to. Contact-center PGs use it. Do not put every phone on the publisher just to be near it.
Administrative XML. How tools create CUCM objects. A bad AXL script is how you get a thousand wrong CSSs.

Realtime Information Service. It is how Unified CM reports whether a phone is registered, and to which node. A phone that is unregistered here never reached CallManager, so start with DHCP, TFTP, and the trust list before you rebuild a route pattern.
Unified CM performance counters, including location bandwidth. A counter that says out of bandwidth is CAC. It is not a DSCP mark.
The Unified CM site where you activate services and turn on traces. ILS will not appear as an active service in Administration until it is activated there.
Who changed a route pattern. Read it before you blame a carrier.
What still references an object. Delete a partition only after dependency records are empty.
Partitions are searched in the order listed. The first match wins. Put the more specific partition first when names overlap.
The directory number CSS is searched before the device CSS. Release 15 MLPP chapter.
The combined partition list limit, including separators. Long partition names reduce how many fit.
Long partition names burn the 1024-character CSS budget faster, so fewer partitions fit. The Release 15 table is drawn in T1-R01.
An empty calling search space. The phone can dial almost nothing, including, if you were careless, emergency.
Patterns with no partition. They are reachable from every CSS. Dangerous for anything except what you truly want global.
The same idea as a null partition. Easy to leave a route pattern there by accident.
The route option that rejects a match. Use it for class-of-service denials you want to control, instead of hoping the CSS is empty.
On a route pattern, whether Unified CM routes the call or blocks it. A block has to be at least as specific as the route it is meant to stop.
On-net or off-net. Affects forwarding and some features. Set it on purpose on the route pattern.
A call that leaves toward the PSTN. Forwarding loops are often an off-net pattern that can reach itself.
A call that stays inside the organization, even if it crosses a WAN. Off-net is the classification that can give a second dial tone after an access code.
A route-pattern checkbox that changes the tone after a steering digit. Cosmetic, and a clue that the pattern matched.
FAC. Stored so you can see who placed the call. It is not encryption.
Client Matter Code, CMC. A project code the caller enters. It is not a class of service and it is not a partition.
A Unified CM object for hours, such as 08:00 to 17:00, built under Call Routing > Class of Control > Time Period. A time schedule is the set of periods a partition uses.
A time period that is active regardless of clock, useful in a test. Remember to turn it off.

cards.term: Route next hop by calling party
cards.def: A CUCM feature that picks the next route based on who called. Easy to forget during a DNA test placed from the wrong phone.
The mask on a calling party transformation pattern. It changes what the carrier or the next hop sees as the caller, after the route has already been chosen.
The mask that rewrites the dialed number on the way out.
Digits inserted after a discard instruction on a translation or transformation. Prefix + after PreDot is the usual globalization step.
Drops every digit before the dot. The dot itself is not dialed. A pattern with no dot has nothing for PreDot to discard.
The named discard on a translation or route pattern, such as PreDot or a fixed number of digits. Prefix digits are applied after the discard.
The CUCM gateway setting that strips the carrier's number down to the extension.
An old IOS number expansion. Prefer translation rules you can test.
All voice codecs, plus VAD, and no DTMF relay. The reason explicit peers exist.
People often leave a default class in place. Name yours for the job, such as g711-only, so the next person sees the policy.
What dial-peer 0 does. Providers answer 488 when the list is nonsense to them.
Forcing one codec so you know what CAC deducted. A region of G.729 and a CUBE offering G.711 will not stay G.729.
Changing video bit rate. A transcoder does not always do this. Do not promise it without the DSP datasheet.
Digital signal processor. Hardware for transcoding and conferences on a gateway. A router without DSPs cannot transcode.
The DSP module family. Capacity is a datasheet number. TODO-verify for the module you own.
Not a codec. People say LTE-AAC. If you did not read the region page, do not list it as allowed.
T.38 or similar. A voice codec class that excludes it will break fax. A different ticket from one-way audio.
An alternative to T.38. Pick the one the carrier asked for.
A DSP function. One-way audio is usually not echo. Echo is hearing yourself.
How many milliseconds of audio sit in one RTP packet. 20 ms is the usual G.711 default people assume. Re-check before you size from it.
A common G.711 packet time. The PA's 16 kbps overhead figure assumes the overhead model in that chapter, which you should re-read if you change packet time.
The 16 kbps the PA adds to a 64 kbps codec to reach 80 kbps. It is not Ethernet overhead.
Ethernet or WAN headers the PA's 80 kbps figure does not include. Size the queue under the policer anyway.
Kilobits per second. Location bandwidth is entered in this unit. Do not type megabits into a field that wants kilobits.
On a location link, the static cost LBM uses to pick a path. It does not track routing-protocol cost.
The location-link path LBM chose. If it is not the WAN you meant, the weight is wrong.
A location setting that deletes CAC for that link. Calls set up and the queue drops them.
A CUCM setting that can treat a video call as desktop or immersive. It changes which pool and which DSCP story you are in.
Room systems the PA marks as prioritized video, AF41.
The PA's opportunistic class when you keep AF42. Soft clients often land here.
Still EF in the PA, and still an audio-pool deduction when the service parameter is true.
Why some older endpoints marked voice and video the same. The PA splits them on purpose and then requires the deduct parameter.
Changing DSCP at the switch because the client cannot be trusted.
Not a standard object in this lab. If a design uses a vendor word you have not cited, leave it out.
A drawing of requests and responses on one or two legs. The lab on this site builds one without a router.
Both directions silent. Often a pinhole, a wrong IP in SDP, or a firewall.
The caller hears ringing. If it never connects, the far end or the queue has the call.
Connected, no audio, no tone. SDP and RTP, not the CSS.
The tone for a failed setup. Capture where analysis stopped before you change codecs.
Often a translation that did not consume the digits, or a pattern that expects more input.
Digits sent as they are dialed, common on some PRIs. CUCM overlap receiving is a separate feature. TODO-verify the Release 15 checkbox before you enable it from memory.
All digits arrive at once. SIP calls from a phone are usually enbloc.
Digits after connect, for an IVR reached through CUCM. Different from the digits that selected the route.
Interactive voice response. In the reference design that is CVP. In Unity it is a call handler. Do not mix the traces.
A greeting that asks you to press a key. Unity Opening Greeting is one. A contact-center script is another.
The number that enters a service: voicemail, hunt, or contact center. Always ask which pilot.
Direct inward dial. A public number mapped to an extension.
Direct outward dial. The calling number you present to the PSTN. A transformation at the trunk is where that presentation is chosen.
Automatic number identification. The calling number on a traditional trunk. SIP carries it in From or PAI.
Dialed number identification. The called number the trunk delivered.
Redirecting number. The original target of a forward. Unity needs this.
CUCM's name for the number that was first dialed before forwards.
The extension that most recently forwarded. Attempt Forward cares about the user extension.
How long a line rings before Call Forward No Answer. It is not T302, and it is not the SRST connection monitor duration.
Interdigit timer. Re-check the milliseconds on the 15SU you run.
How many calls a line accepts before it is busy. A trigger of 1 sends the second call to forward.
The line's call cap, paired with the busy trigger.
Two calls on one DN. Contact-center agents often need a second line for transfers. The design guide discusses single-line and multi-line.
An agent phone with more than one line. Confirm the UCCE support notes before you enable every line.
The simpler UCCE phone. Transfers may need a second line or a CTI-controlled transfer.
The template that decides whether a second line exists.
A supervisor's set of agents. Not a skill group, though people nest them.
A CUCM or Unity administrative boundary in multitenant systems. Not a partition by itself.
A short prefix for on-net dialing between offices, translated to +E.164.
The digit that means 'this is a site code.' Discard it in the translation.
On-net dialing that uses ! because extensions differ in length. Urgent patterns protect emergency numbers from the wait.
A pattern of X's that completes as soon as the digits arrive. No timer.
Matches exactly one digit, 0 through 9. It does not match a plus sign. Use a backslash-plus when the plus is a dialed character.
Matches one or more digits and can wait for more. That wait is why 911 must be urgent, so a variable-length pattern does not hold the emergency call.
The dot in a route pattern is the PreDot delimiter, not a digit match. Discard Digits PreDot drops everything before that dot. A pattern may contain one dot.
A character class such as [2-9] in a pattern. The route-pattern lab's educational matcher treats a simple range.
North American Numbering Plan. The @ wildcard is about this plan.
The ITU numbering plan. +E.164 is the form this lab globalizes to.
The digits after + that select a country. 1 is the NANP country code.
The number inside a country, without the country code.
Turning a local dialing habit into +E.164 before the route pattern, then localizing again at the trunk if the carrier requires it.
Turning +E.164 into the digits a carrier or a user expects.
The gateway or trunk a call leaves on. In a centralized plan that is often the route group selected by Standard Local Route Group.
Where the call entered: a phone, a gateway, or a trunk.
A call that enters a border and leaves the same border. Diversion headers die here when a profile is careless.
Forward hop counts and translation CSSs that cannot see themselves.
CUCM's limit on how many times a call can forward. A loop hits it and fails.
The same pattern matching forever. Fix the CSS on the translation, not the carrier.
A CSS you put on a translation so the second lookup can only see the patterns you intend.
The CSS a translation or a call-forward uses for the following lookup.
The line CSS plus the device CSS that started the call. A translation then continues with the CSS configured on the translation, which can be a different list.
The called device. Its CSS does not choose the caller's route.
On a trunk, the CSS applied to calls arriving from that trunk.
People say this and mean the line CSS or a rerouting CSS. Ask which page they are looking at.
The inbound calling search space on a SIP trunk.
Editing headers. CUCM uses scripts. CUBE uses SIP profiles. Both can delete Diversion.
A SIP profile that copies one header to another. Useful, and a way to leak an internal number.
PAI or PPI. What you are allowed to claim as the caller.
P-Preferred-Identity. Weaker than PAI. Know which one the carrier honors.
An older calling-number header. Some carriers still want it. Do not add it everywhere.
Where CUCM can place a HELD location URI. Emergency, not a contact-center variable.
The RedSky identifier Webex Calling stores in Control Hub, with a secret.
The phone's HTTPS call to the location server. A failure here means the INVITE may go out without a location.
Not a Unity handler. The CUCM and CER path for 911. Keep the names apart in an outage.
A route pattern for 911, urgent, in a partition on the device CSS.
More than one ELIN on an ERL so two simultaneous emergencies do not share a callback. Capacity per ERL stays TODO-verify.
The ELIN the PSAP dials back. It must land at the right site.
A typical on-site notification target under Kari's Law. The statute requires that someone on site be notified. It does not name this desk.
One way to tell the security desk. Confirm it is actually watched.
A test number some providers publish. Confirm it for the carrier you use. This lab does not claim every carrier answers 933.
The NANP emergency number. Other countries differ. Do not hard-code it into a Unity caller-input key.
A prefixed emergency number. Kari's Law says users must be able to dial 911 without the prefix. You may still accept 9911.
A steering digit. Stripping it is normal. Stripping it from 911 is not, unless a translation immediately produces a real emergency route.
Put the emergency partition on the phone, not only on the line.
A restrictive line CSS is fine if the device CSS still contains 911.
CER can map an IP subnet to an ERL when switch-port tracking is not available. Soft clients need a better plan.
The Ethernet port CER tracks. Move the phone, move the ERL, if tracking is on.
How CER often reads switch CAM tables. A blocked SNMP community looks like every phone in the default ERL.
CER or CUCM telling a local party. Kari's Law cares that a human notices.
The return call to the ELIN. Route it to the site, not to a generic auto attendant that cannot find the caller.
How fast the provider learns a new ELIN address. The delay is theirs. Do not restart CUCM to speed it up.
The carrier that delivers the emergency call. CER has provider-specific guides. The 14 guide is older than 12 months if you are on it. Re-check.
A national emergency provider people still name. Confirm the current provider in the CER guide you are following.
The credential paired with the company ID. Treat it as a secret. Do not put it in a screenshot in this repo.
An ERL is a place, such as a floor or a switch-port group, that emergency responders can be sent to. An ELIN is the callback number that represents that place.
Part of a dispatchable location inside a building. A street address alone can be insufficient.
A dispatchable-location detail under RAY BAUM'S Act, along with floor or room. A street address alone is not the whole duty when the caller is inside a multi-tenant building.
Latitude and longitude. Some location objects carry both. Do not invent precision.
Often unknown unless the client or the user supplies it. Off-premises rules apply.
An outside client calling 911 may be nowhere near the campus ELIN. Do not present the headquarters callback for a traveler.
A VPN phone looks internal and may inherit the campus ERL while the human is elsewhere. That is a known class of misroute.
The location reference placed in signaling. If it is empty, the call may still complete and still be non-compliant.
Direct dial, notification, and a dispatchable location. A working route pattern is only the first of those.
911 that needs a prefix, or a call with no usable location, or no on-site notice.
16 February 2020 for Kari's Law applicability to new installs. 6 January 2021 and 6 January 2022 for the location classes.
The Kari's Law trigger. Whether a core upgrade restarts that clock stays TODO-verify.
Also a Kari's Law trigger, along with imported, sold, or leased.
The on-site half of Kari's Law: someone at the site must be told that 911 was dialed. A route pattern alone does not do that.
911 with no access code, which is the Kari's Law dialing duty. A route pattern that still requires 9 does not meet that duty.
What Kari's Law removes. Users must not need the 9.
A notification target. Name a person or a desk, not a shared mailbox nobody reads.
Notification still has to reach a human. A closed greeting is not a security desk.
A misroute. The contact-center pattern must not be more attractive than the urgent emergency pattern.
